papers.title: Hip dysplasia in patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty in a major centre in New Zealand
papers.abstract: aim: The aim of this study was to determine the absolute number of total hip arthroplasties (THA) performed in a single centre for patients whose pre-operative radiographs demonstrated evidence of hip dysplasia. methods: We retrospectively analysed 317 consecutive primary THA cases at Dunedin Hospital. Pre-operative radiographs were reviewed using standardised measurements: lateral centre-edge angle (LCEA), Tönnis angle (TA), acetabular quotient (AQ) and crossover sign. results: Overall, 21% had dysplastic TA (>10 degrees), increasing to 30% in those <60 years. Severe under-coverage (LCEA <20 degrees) was present in 8% overall and 17% of patients <60, while mild under-coverage (LCEA 20–25 degrees) occurred in 15%. A pathological AQ (<250) was found in 29% of all patients, rising to 38% in those <65 years. Among evaluable radiographs, 18% showed a positive crossover sign, indicating acetabular retroversion. conclusion: Developmental dysplasia of the hip was present in up to one-third of THA patients, over 10 times the rate recorded in the New Zealand Joint Registry. These findings highlight the likelihood of underdiagnosed dysplasia in patients undergoing THA for osteoarthritis. Recognition of subtle dysplastic features, coupled with refined registry coding and potential adjustments to screening policy, may improve early detection and preventative strategies aimed at delaying or avoiding joint replacement.

papers.title: Electrostatic Remodeling of the Plasma Membrane Enables Caveolae-Mediated ZIF8 Delivery for Bone Regeneration.
papers.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks offer powerful platforms for intracellular delivery and tissue regeneration, yet their membrane-level interactions are poorly defined. Here, we show that cationic zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF8) remodels the electrostatic landscape of the anionic plasma membrane, triggering caveolae-dependent endocytosis and promoting the intracellular delivery for bone regeneration. ζ-potential analysis and Kelvin probe force microscopy demonstrated that ZIF8 rapidly increased membrane surface electrostatics and induced localized electrostatic polarization at the nanobio interface. Simulations and adsorption kinetics revealed rapid saturation and a strong pH dependence, supporting a charge-dominated adsorption mechanism. Transmission electron microscopy captured sequential uptake events, including caveolae formation, membrane invagination, and lysosomal trafficking. Transcriptomics further identified CAV2-associated endocytosis and mechanosensitive fluid shear-stress pathways as key contributors. On the basis of this mechanism, we constructed an OGP-loaded ZIF8 coating on polyethyleneimine-functionalized titanium implants, enabling intracellular peptide delivery, partial lysosomal escape, enhanced osteogenesis, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses, and improved osseointegration in rat bone defect models.

papers.title: cuRoboV2-Fast: Fast Torque-Limited Collision-Free Motion Planning
papers.abstract: We present cuRoboV2-Fast, a GPU-accelerated planner that reduces both planning latency and execution time for collision-free, payload-aware, torque-limited motions. B-spline trajectory optimization reduces the required iterations, while accelerated robot computations and differentiable inverse dynamics reduce refinement cost and accommodate changing payloads. TimeOpt optimizes traversal speed along the fixed path under sampled velocity, acceleration, jerk, and torque constraints, exploiting local spline support to solve banded Newton systems efficiently on the GPU. With a 3,kg payload, cuRoboV2-Fast achieves 4.4 ms mean planning time on RTX 5090, 14.7x faster than cuRoboV2. Our method on Jetson AGX Orin plans faster than cuRoboV1 + TOPPRA on RTX 5090. A stereo-camera-based deployment on YAM achieves 5.93 s mean completed pick-and-drop cycles, 34.6% shorter than cuRoboV2. Code (Apache 2.0): www.github.com/NVlabs/curobo , Project Page: www.research.nvidia.com/labs/lpr/curobov2-fast .

papers.title: Motion-guided Contrastive Regularization For Latent World Models
papers.abstract: JEPA-style world models learn action-conditioned latent dynamics without reconstructing observations, but distributional regularization alone does not ensure that their representations preserve information needed for control. We identify static collapse, a failure mode in which the encoder preserves episode-specific static content while suppressing manipulation-relevant state changes. Because static content is temporally predictable yet diverse across episodes, this failure can persist despite regularizers such as SIGReg. A controlled study on OGBench-Cube shows that introducing randomized backgrounds substantially degrades planning performance while leaving the underlying manipulation task unchanged. To address this problem, we propose motion-guided contrastive regularization. Our approach compares predicted latent transitions with transitions to candidate observations from the same episode, reducing the usefulness of static background identity for distinguishing action outcomes. Optical-flow similarities provide soft contrastive targets, allowing candidates with similar motion to receive similar supervision. Combined with latent prediction and SIGReg, our objective encourages representations to preserve within-episode state distinctions and similarities between related transitions. Our method improves planning success over LeWorldModel (LeWM) from 52% to 78% on OGBench-Cube with randomized backgrounds and from 14% to 54% on LIBERO-Object, while maintaining comparable performance on four other visual-control benchmarks.

papers.title: ALTO: African and Levantine Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence Corpus
papers.abstract: Tech-facilitated gender based violence (TFGBV) is a pervasive online harm affecting women and gender minority groups through its many direct and covert forms. Current models and annotated datasets for gendered harm detection are dominated by data from, and models trained in, Global North languages. In collaboration with civil society organizations (CSOs) from Jordan, Francophone West Africa, and Kenya, we developed a community-led approach to crowdsource culturally and linguistically relevant instances of TFGBV in Levantine Arabic, African French, and Swahili. We annotated the crowdsourced data using active learning to develop a small but performant dataset (N=3022) called ALTO to improve TFGBV detection in the three languages. Through benchmarking and fine-tuning experiments, we show that existing harmful content detection models show poor TFGBV recall within ALTO and improve with fine-tuning. We found that models often miss covert harms across all languages, while error rates are markedly higher in Swahili. We report the experimental results and release the annotation taxonomy, dataset, and trained models.

papers.title: From Certified Pairs to a Certified Hub: Reasoner-Checked Crosswalks for the Information Exchange Standard
papers.abstract: A national digital twin was conceived as an ecosystem of twins connected through mappings to a common foundation, but the roadmap that promises to confirm those mappings are valid never says what valid means. We give the test a precise form, coherence and conservativity of the merged ontology, borrowed from logic-based alignment repair, and apply it to the Information Exchange Standard (IES), first pair by pair and then to whole hubs. Crosswalks from IES into thirteen ontologies across seven sector groups, anchored on the building ontologies BOT, Brick, and SAREF4BLDG, pass through separate stages of matching, human review, certification of each SKOS correspondence against the two class hierarchies, and reasoning with HermiT. Pair by pair, the stages catch different failures: certification alone removed all 526 conservativity violations of the raw crosswalks, review alone left 73, and together they made eleven of twelve overlapping pairs coherent and conservative. Pairwise certification does not compose. Merging the three certified building crosswalks into one hub made five Brick classes unsatisfiable, through a homonym between the IES and Brick notions of a floor that only BOT's disjointness axioms expose; rejecting that one row gave a coherent and conservative hub that entails 290 cross-ontology links nobody wrote down. The core hub is inconsistent before any crosswalk is added, because two published standards, the Open Energy Ontology and BFO 2020, contradict each other; with either one left out it is coherent and conservative. A hub, not a pair, is the unit an ecosystem of twins has to certify.

papers.title: Dynamic Shape Control of Soft Trunk Robots
papers.abstract: Controlling the shape profile of soft trunk robots extends their reach into complex regions of the workspace and enhances their use in practical applications. Recent advances in soft robot design have enabled soft trunk robots to achieve greater flexibility in conforming to complex shapes. Specifically, trunk robots whose geometries are designed as helicoids have been shown to enable extreme shape-changing capabilities. Their compliance makes them highly nonlinear, which in turn makes shape control difficult. On similar tendon-driven trunk robots, model-based controllers based on the theory of adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs) have achieved high accuracy in closed-loop end-effector tracking. We extend this approach by learning an aSSM model of the full body of a trimmed-helicoid soft trunk robot from data and use this in a model predictive control (MPC) scheme to demonstrate a range of shape control tasks on hardware. On closed-loop dynamic shape regulation, our method outperforms the available linear baselines by a factor of 10. In human-in-the-loop interactive demos, our method completes section-by-section shaping and balances a tennis ball for over 25 seconds, while the linear baselines fall short. A model-free reinforcement learning policy trained for 12 hours on hardware fails on the same balancing task. These results establish aSSM-based MPC as a practical route to full-body shape control on real soft hardware.

papers.title: Amortized Optimization for Calibrating Stochastic Social Simulators
papers.abstract: Stochastic simulators need suitable parameter values to reproduce observed behaviour in complex systems. Searching for these values through repeated simulations makes frequent recalibration computationally expensive. We develop an amortized optimizer that uses simulations collected in advance to learn how to choose parameters that make simulated outcomes agree with observations. Once fitted, it maps new observations to feasible parameters without further simulator calls. The method retains alternative parameter settings that can explain similar observations and compares their responses, avoiding the conflicting labels that arise when training a single parameter regressor. Historical observations also provide supervision by showing which simulated responses agree with the data, even when the underlying parameters are unknown. Experiments across four simulators compare calibration accuracy and query time. Dedicated cost analyses quantify traffic preparation and the recorded financial reuse costs.On new traffic targets, local correction more than halves query time relative to empirical and surrogate selection; a learned inverse is faster still, with similar mean error. In a retrospective comparison on real financial data, our method returns parameters about $1.07\times10^{7}$ times faster than a 10-minute Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization search, with mean calibration error 3.06% higher. Reusing simulation work across observations supports repeated parameter updates when the available time is too short for a new search.

papers.title: Playing Soccer Like Humans Do: Learning Versatile and Agile Humanoid Soccer via Latent Motion Priors
papers.abstract: Humanoid soccer requires a robot to seamlessly combine agile locomotion, ball manipulation, and impact-rich contact dynamics across a continuous, dynamic behavioral spectrum. Yet existing approaches either cover only a limited set of skills, or forego motion priors entirely and produce unnatural behaviors, leaving the combination of a unified skill set and human-like motion quality unaddressed. We present soccerbot, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that resolves both limitations through a structured latent motion prior distilled from large-scale human soccer motion capture data. By constraining policy learning within this dynamically plausible motion manifold, a single skill-conditioned policy naturally learns to perform moving, dribbling, trapping, and kicking in a unified formulation, while inherently producing human-like motion and fluid transitions during commanded skill switching. Augmented by robustness-oriented simulation design, soccerbot transfers zero-shot to the Unitree G1 humanoid robot, demonstrating agile, natural, and robust execution of the full soccer skill repertoire under real-world conditions.

papers.title: RAGAM-AI: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning based Agentic approach powered by Generative AI for Edge Resource Management
papers.abstract: Resource management for distributed edge networks hosting different services has been handled efficiently using Reinforcement learning (RL). Reward generalization in complex workflows is still an open issue within the RL realm. Therefore, this work proposes RAGAM-AI, a hybrid framework that combines the capabilities of RL algorithms and Generative-AI (Gen-AI) for powering an Agentic AI workflow that optimizes resource allocation at the Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) units. This framework further resolves the reward generalization issue by utilizing Large Language Model (LLM) for feedback. A Multi- Agent Soft-Actor Critic (MASAC) using MathΣtral as a reward oracle is implemented for managing resource allocations at the MEC. RAGAM-AI interprets system state information and evaluates multi-objective trade-offs guiding the resource orchestration loop over distributed edge server agents. The complexity of the framework is further brought down by incorporating surrogate reward model. The overall performance is evaluated against the single agent SAC, REINFORCE and random policies for benchmarking. On using RAGAM-AI, lower allocation deviations for CPU, memory and bandwidth resources are reported while minimizing the latency and data rate costs. A scalable AI as a feedback (AIAF) solution optimizing network resources with significant performance improvement is thus presented.

papers.title: MKD2World: A Typed Spatial MarkDown World Model For Web Agents
papers.abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents can improve decision-making with world-model foresight, provided that predicted states accurately reflect post-action interfaces. Existing state representations fail to jointly capture interface layout, UI semantics, and explicit locations. We introduce Typed Spatial Markdown (TSM), a Markdown-style textual state representation for desktop web interfaces. TSM serializes block-level and atomic-level UI elements according to their spatial relationships, jointly encoding their types, visual semantics, explicit locations, optional control states, and hierarchical membership. To train a screenshot-to-TSM renderer, we construct AtomBlock-WebUI, a dataset with precise annotations at both granularities. By injecting element-type labels into HTML and directly extracting bounding boxes after rendering, we avoid annotation errors caused by post-hoc inference from webpage structures. Building on TSM, we propose MKD2World, a desktop web world model trained in two stages for current-state description and action-conditioned next-state prediction. During inference, the web agent queries MKD2World as needed and performs a ``digest'' step, in which it interprets each predicted state and extracts task-relevant evidence for selecting the best action. Experiments show that MKD2World-9B achieves an EleF1 score of 26.50 on the out-of-domain test set, outperforming GPT-5.6-Sol(14.98) by 11.52 points. Across Online-Mind2Web tasks, MKD2World-9B improves the success rate of the Qwen3.5-35B web agent from 22.94% to 37.61%, achieving competitive performance among leading open-source GUI world models. Code is available at https://github.com/OmniAI-Lab-CUHKSZ/MKD2World.

papers.title: Microdroplet Generator Surrogate Enhancement and Inverse Design Through an Uncertainty-Guided Framework
papers.abstract: Microfluidic droplet generation is critical for many applications, yet efficient device design in high-dimensional parameter spaces remains computationally prohibitive due to complex multiphase flow dynamics. This work presents a unified methodology that couples adaptive surrogate enhancement with simulation-driven inverse design. High-fidelity Volume-of-Fluid simulations provide ground-truth data, while neural network ensembles predict flow regimes and droplet diameters. Ensemble-based uncertainty quantification identifies epistemic uncertainty using consensus levels for regime classification and the coefficient of variation for diameter prediction, revealing that uncertainty concentrates near regime transition boundaries where physics is highly sensitive to parameter perturbations. A physics-informed enrichment strategy targets these critical zones and addresses class imbalances by deploying additional targeted simulations and retraining the surrogates forming the ensembles. A framework that integrates Particle Swarm Optimization for constrained inverse design, balancing accuracy with predictive confidence and physical consistency is therefore proposed. Validation on independent test datasets demonstrates that the enriched ensembles achieve higher accuracy, with the fraction of predictions within the 0-3% error range on droplet diameter nearly doubling, and high-error cases (above 10%) dropping substantially. The inverse design procedure reliably identifies physically realizable configurations meeting target droplet sizes. This approach significantly reduces computational costs while ensuring reliable predictions, offering a framework with potential applicability to the optimization of a broad range of microfluidic systems.

papers.abstract: Online reinforcement learning offers an effective approach to precise laboratory manipulation, yet costly real-world demonstrations and limited access to dense process rewards hinder its practical application. Here, simulator states provide task events and geometric progress under physical prerequisites and ordering constraints, yielding rewards for policy pretraining with simulated demonstrations and reinforcement learning. We distill this supervision into a visual reward model. During real-world interaction, its predictions are combined with execution history to compute dense rewards for human-in-the-loop policy refinement. Across five real-world laboratory tasks, TwinBridge achieves a final mean autonomous success rate of 98% with at most 25 minutes of real-world interaction per task. Experiments show that dense rewards improve interaction efficiency over sparse rewards, and simulation-based policy initialization further accelerates learning.

papers.title: KolTa: A Physics-Informed Active Learning Framework for Formulation Discovery with Limited Data
papers.abstract: Finding high-performing formulations is difficult when few have been measured and experimental budgets are limited. We propose KolTa, an active learning framework that selects batches to discover the top 5% of formulations at a target temperature under a fixed query budget. KolTa combines a three-stage predictor of component contributions, role-conditioned interactions, and anchored temperature response with task-specific soft physics constraints. Its Physics-Residual-Calibrated Upper Confidence Bound (PRC-UCB) acquisition rule combines predicted utility, ensemble disagreement, and a target-temperature physics residual, with nonnegative exploration weights fitted to out-of-fold signed errors. We evaluate the framework on three measured tasks and one simulated task covering binary-mixture viscosity, drug solubility, ionic-liquid viscosity, and electrolyte conductivity. KolTa ranks first or second in mean area under the learning curve (AULC) on every task and outperforms seven of the eight comparator strategies in paired tests, winning 75 of 78 paired comparisons across tasks and seeds against those seven strategies. Across the three measured tasks, its largest gap to the best mean AULC is 0.032, compared with at least 0.056 for every comparator. On Drug, reaching 80% average recovery of the remaining targets across drugs requires an estimated median of 348 additional formulation queries, about 18% fewer than the fastest comparator. Researchers can adapt the framework to diverse formulation problems through component roles and physical constraints.

papers.title: Vortex-Induced Torque in Grasping Soft Objects: Influence of Geometry and Pneumatic Parameters
papers.abstract: Vortex grippers are commonly integrated into automated systems for handling objects with complex geometries in packaging, sorting, and assembling. However, their interaction with compliant objects remains difficult to predict, particularly with respect to the vortex-induced torque transmitted during grasping. This study investigates vortex-induced torque during the grasping of compliant objects and quantifies the coupled effects of supply pressure, tangential nozzle diameter, surface geometry, and curvature. The results show that increasing the tangential nozzle diameter primarily enhances the sensitivity of the generated torque to supply pressure rather than producing a uniformly higher torque. Surface geometry also strongly influences the rotational interaction, with dome-concave surfaces generally producing substantially greater torque than corresponding dome-convex surfaces, whereas the difference between cylindrical concave and convex surfaces is comparatively small. The strongest and most repeatable response was observed for a dome-concave surface exhibiting favorable object-gripper geometric matching. Among the evaluated machine-learning regression methods, Gaussian Process Regression provided the best overall predictive performance under repeated cross-validation, demonstrating that vortex-induced torque can be estimated from combined pneumatic and geometric parameters. These findings provide a basis for predicting and utilizing vortex-induced torque in the dexterous manipulation of soft objects.

papers.title: Traffic-VL: Reinforced Vision-Language Models for Generalizable End-to-End Traffic Signal Control
papers.abstract: Existing traffic signal control methods typically rely on structured traffic states produced by dedicated perception pipelines. Emerging visual approaches often use idealized simulator images and convert them into intermediate representations before control, limiting their ability to directly exploit roadside visual observations. SynTra-V converts physics-based traffic simulations into photorealistic multi-view surveillance imagery across diverse road topologies and sensing conditions, and automatic semantic auditing checks that control-critical geometry, vehicle movements, and lane semantics match the simulator state. Traffic-VL is an eight-billion-parameter vision-language model that directly maps synchronized multi-view images and natural-language phase descriptions to signal decisions without intermediate structured states. Building on Traffic-R1's two-stage reinforced reasoning framework, Traffic-VL adapts its vision encoder via offline reinforcement learning on SynTra-V and freezes it during online visual stepwise trajectory policy optimization in closed-loop simulation. Experiments show that Traffic-VL matches structured-state Traffic-R1 while outperforming image-based controllers and general-purpose vision-language models, including Gemini 3 Pro. Evaluations on unseen topologies, degraded sensing conditions, real surveillance footage, and a three-week deployment across ten intersections further demonstrate robust visual generalization and effective constrained online control.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction for Distribution-to-Distribution Regression
papers.abstract: Conformal Prediction (CP) provides a model-agnostic framework for constructing finite-sample prediction sets with coverage guarantees and has become a tool for reliable decision-making in high-risk settings. Recent advances have extended Split Conformal Prediction to increasingly complex learning problems, including multilabel, high-dimensional, and functional outputs. In this work, we study CP for Distribution-to-Distribution Regression, a setting of growing interest across many application domains. We show that a naive application of Split CP yields prediction sets that, while marginally valid, are non-interpretable, e.g., lacking a well-defined volume or a tractable sampling procedure, and of limited practical value. To overcome this, we propose a new conformal framework that operates in an orthogonal basis space, producing interpretable prediction sets while preserving coverage guarantees. We further develop an adaptive variant with asymptotic conditional coverage under mild assumptions. Empirical results on synthetic and real-world datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/tuanhacs/conformal_d2d.

papers.title: Beyond Terminal Constraints: Reliable Robot Control with Learned Safe Sets
papers.abstract: Ensuring safety in advanced robot control methods such as Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Reinforcement Learning remains an open challenge. A common approach relies on control-invariant sets, yet their exact computation for nonlinear systems is generally intractable, and numerical approximations compromise theoretical guarantees. In this work, we show that safety does not need to rely exclusively on control invariance. We introduce novel classes of safe sets, each broader than classical control-invariant sets, and analyze corresponding MPC schemes that guarantee recursive feasibility by constraining different nodes of the prediction horizon rather than only the terminal state. Furthermore, when the safe set is an inner approximation of a suitable control-invariant set, our methods can ensure safety through a safe-abort strategy, even in the absence of recursive feasibility. We validate our approaches in extensive simulations on a 6-joint robot manipulator, showing fewer constraint violations than state-of-the-art methods while maintaining comparable tracking performance and computational efficiency. Hardware experiments further demonstrate the practicality of our schemes for real-world robotic applications.

Given an initial image and a scene-description prompt, the model generates video conditioned on temporally aligned camera and hand controls. Causal adaptation and few-step distillation support chunk-level online generation, allowing users to update their controls based on generated visual feedback. We further introduce TouchéBench to evaluate hand-motion following, camera--hand coordination, online interaction, and object response. Together, these components establish a framework for studying continuous exploration and hand-driven interaction within generative worlds.

papers.title: InterSim: Innovative Intersection Digital Twins for Human-in-the-Loop Driving Simulation

InterSim links the real world and the simulation world through two closed cycles: a digital twin cycle that builds each intersection twin from agency design and traffic data and returns evidence from simulation to the agency, and an HITL cycle in which human drivers or automated driving algorithms operate the ego vehicle under identical scenario conditions. The research capabilities of InterSim are demonstrated through two case studies: a surrogate safety study compares post-encroachment time distributions between a Reduced Conflict Intersection and a standard intersection under different traffic volumes; an eco-driving study compares human drivers with a rule-based agent using vehicle-to-infrastructure information and reveals differences in emission and driving behavior. These studies demonstrate that InterSim provides a reusable digital twin platform for investigating innovative intersection designs from diverse perspectives. Demo video and open-source code can be accessed at https://purduedigitaltwin.github.io/InterSim/

papers.title: CellCanon: An Agentic Cellular World Model for Prediction, Explanation, and Observation-Driven Updating
papers.abstract: Biological discovery requires using molecular knowledge and new measurements to infer responses beyond the conditions already observed. We introduce CellCanon, the first agentic cellular world model to unify single-cell expression prediction, evidence-grounded explanation, and observation-driven updating. Its predictive core reuses condition-level biological evidence across gene-specific numerical readouts to guide single-cell expression generation. A shared world state links predictions, acquired measurements, and source-linked claims, supporting explanation and revision. On 339 held-out SciPlex3 conditions across three cell lines, CellCanon improves differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 over the best baseline for each metric by 63.3% and 17.3%, respectively, and direction Macro-F1 by 7.2%. Relative to gene-wise reasoning on matched drug-cell cohorts, measured language-model token use falls by 99.77% for Predict and 98.41% for Explain. On the source-grounded benchmark, Explain correctly answers all answerable questions with supporting proofs and identifies all insufficient-evidence cases. In simulated experimental feedback, Update uses one measured source context per drug to exceed the best fine-tuned baselines in differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 without changing model weights. Together, these capabilities support a cumulative account of cellular responses, with predictions and biological judgments that can be revised as evidence accumulates.

papers.title: MIGONet: a multiple-input graph neural operator with solver-free discrete manufactured-solution training
papers.abstract: Surrogate modeling of transport requires operators that capture the combined influence of spatially distributed sources and Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, together with training datasets that can be generated at low computational cost. This work presents MIGONet, a multiple-input graph neural operator, and a discrete method of manufactured solutions (MMS) that trains it without solving a partial differential equation, using steady heat conduction as the model problem. In the discrete MMS procedure, temperature fields are prescribed a priori, and the source terms and Dirichlet or Neumann boundary data are evaluated with the same discrete operators as the reference finite-difference method (FDM), so every training sample satisfies the discrete governing equations by construction. Because the boundary data are derived from each field, a Dirichlet or Neumann condition can be assigned to every boundary segment of every sample, and the boundary specification becomes an operator input. MIGONet supplies representations of the complete source field and boundary data to every node before local message passing. On the rectangular domain, it is compared with a version without the complete-source encoder (MIGONet-local) and with the multiple-input operator network MIONet, using the same training data. MIGONet achieves mean relative temperature errors of 10.31% and 10.64% for curved-wire and Gaussian-spot heating, compared with 45.97% and 48.34% for MIONet and 72.25% and 67.82% for MIGONet-local. For 10,000 samples, discrete MMS reduces data-generation time from 486.65 s to 3.15 s relative to matched iterative FDM labeling. Separately trained MIGONet models are also evaluated on L-shaped, disc-shaped, and ring-shaped domains.

papers.title: Time-to-Goal: Learned Temporal Metrics for Long-Horizon Planning with JEPA World Models
papers.abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) support planning by comparing predicted latent states with an encoded goal. For this comparison to guide temporal progress, states closer in time to the goal should receive lower costs. However, training representations for prediction and distribution regularization does not directly enforce this ordering. We examine this mismatch in flat LeWorldModel (LeWM) by analyzing how its Euclidean goal cost changes with temporal separation. Our analysis identifies conditions under which states at different long offsets receive similar average costs, weakening their temporal distinction. To learn the missing ordering explicitly, we introduce Time-to-Goal (T2G), a lightweight metric trained on latent triples from offline trajectories. A margin ranking loss encourages smaller distances for temporally nearer states, requiring no rewards or policy labels. The learned metric then replaces the Euclidean planning cost while the JEPA encoder and predictor remain frozen. Diagnostics on AntMaze and FourRoom show that T2G preserves stronger temporal contrast and improves near--far ranking at long offsets. Across four navigation and manipulation benchmarks, T2G improves the average planning success rate from 32.7\% (flat LeWM) to 63.0\% and approaches or even surpasses the performance of the hierarchical H-JEPA baselines. These results show that learning temporal ordering for the goal cost can substantially improve latent planning even with a flat world model.

papers.title: ZipDrift: Generating Multimodal Short-Horizon MPC Costs with One-Step Drifting Models
papers.abstract: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert. We observe that the optimal correction is often multimodal: when a slower opponent can be passed on either side, good corrections of opposite sign coexist, and the expert's choice between them hinges on tiny cost differences. Deterministic regression then averages modes or inherits inconsistent expert tie-breaking. We propose ZipDrift, which trains a one-step drifting generator over MPC cost corrections, tilted toward low closed-loop cost and learned only from cost evaluations of candidate corrections, without differentiating through the optimiser. A few generated candidates are ranked by a learned critic, and the model-based MPC then enforces dynamics and constraints. In a kinematic overtaking benchmark derived from ZipMPC, 53% of contexts are bimodal and the manual short-horizon MPC crashes in 28.5% of test episodes. With an eight-dimensional stagewise correction, ZipDrift is collision-free in all 600 test episodes and matches the best evaluated candidate, whereas an idealised ZipMPC-style regressor crashes in 4.0% (16.0% with inconsistent expert labels) and critic-ranked random candidates with the same budget in 2.0%.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Adaptive Sampling on a Generative Ocean Model
papers.abstract: Adaptive sampling can substantially improve the value of sparse ocean observations by directing mobile robots toward measurements that are most informative for an evolving environment. Recent learned generative ocean models can produce high-resolution forecasts and ensembles at substantially lower computational cost than traditional numerical models, creating an opportunity to use rich predictive forecasts directly in closed-loop robotic sampling. However, these models do not natively provide the explicit uncertainty representations assumed by classical informative-planning methods, and their forecasts often evolve in learned latent spaces rather than directly in physical ocean variables. We develop a multi-robot closed-loop adaptive sampling framework that uses a single learned generative model for forecasting, uncertainty estimation, planning, and measurement assimilation. The model forecasts an ensemble in latent space, decodes it to physical ocean states, and uses ensemble statistics to construct A- or D-optimal sampling objectives. We select sampling locations subject to robot reachability under predicted currents. The collected measurements are assimilated back into the latent state using observation-conditioned diffusion sampling. Across 120 test scenarios A- and D-optimal sampling generally outperforms static, random, and systematic-coverage baselines while adding little planning overhead. Our experiments uncover several scenarios in which model uncertainty diverges from forecast error, motivating future work in uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Development of a biomimetic hydrogel cervical spinal cord surrogate for transverse compression across loading rates
papers.abstract: Abstract Study Design: Experimental laboratory study; fully factorial hydrogel formulation design with mechanical benchmarking against published spinal cord tissue data. Objectives To develop and characterise polyacrylamide-alginate (PAAm-alginate) double-network hydrogels as surrogates for the transverse compressive response of cervical spinal cord tissue, and to identify the formulation variables governing surrogate stiffness. Setting: University biomechanics laboratory, Adelaide, Australia. Methods Twenty-seven formulations combined three alginate concentrations (4.7, 7.8, 10.3% w/v), three ionic crosslinkers (CaCl₂, FeCl₃, AlCl₃) and three immersion durations (1, 2, 3 h). 313 elliptical specimens were tested in transverse compression at four displacement rates (~ 0.01 to 140 s⁻¹). Characteristic curves were generated by arc-length re-parameterisation, compared by statistical parametric mapping, and benchmarked against published human and porcine cervical cord data. Results All formulations showed J-shaped, rate-dependent viscoelastic responses. Crosslinking ion valency had the greatest influence, trivalent species being approximately five times stiffer than divalent CaCl₂; alginate concentration had a moderate, diminishing effect and immersion duration had little effect beyond 2 h. CaCl₂ formulations matched the benchmarks most closely at every rate; at ~ 50 s⁻¹, CaCl₂ / 10.3% / pooled 2 h + 3 h matched porcine cervical cord in tangent modulus (~ 1180 kPa) and stress at benchmark failure strain (~ 490 kPa). Conclusions PAAm-alginate double-network hydrogels reproduce the nonlinear, rate-dependent transverse compressive behaviour of cervical spinal cord tissue and can be tuned to published benchmarks, most closely under dynamic loading. They provide a basis for instrumentable cord surrogates for ex vivo injury biomechanics and surgical simulation. Sponsorship: University of Adelaide Medical School Development Grant.

papers.title: Health resource utilization and direct procedural costs of arthroplasty surgery: a retrospective cost analysis
papers.abstract: Background As osteoarthritis becomes more prevalent, demand for procedures such as total knee arthroplasty (TKA), total hip arthroplasty (THA), and other joint replacement procedures is rising. Understanding the cost drivers and patient demographics is important for maintaining financial sustainability while ensuring optimal patient care. This study aims to determine the costs associated with various arthroplasty procedures, analyze comparison of costs between different arthroplasty procedures, and fill the gap in the local literature regarding direct cost burden of arthroplasty surgery in Saudi Arabia. Methods This retrospective study included 1,833 patients who underwent arthroplasty procedures. The costs were converted into USD, and their trends over time were analyzed. Statistical analyses, including independent samples t tests and chi-square tests, were used to compare costs across procedures, age groups, and sex. The projection analysis was applied to project the number procedures and expected costs for 2030. Results The total expenditures for the study period exceeded $25 million, with TKA accounting for 65% of the total cost. Female patients composed 74.7% of the patient population, and male patients were generally older. TKA had the highest total cost at $16,632,000 and the greatest number of cases at 1,386. The highest average cost was for hip revision arthroplasty at $18,666.67, followed by shoulder arthroplasty at $16,533.33. By 2030, arthroplasty cases are projected to increase 3-fold, with the total cost rising to $20.87 million compared with 2021. Conclusion The total expenditures of arthroplasty procedures, particularly TKA, are significant, with the costs projected to increase by 2030. Strategic planning, including expanding infrastructure, optimizing resources, and adopting cost-saving measures such as bulk purchasing, will be crucial to maintaining high-quality patient care while addressing the increased demand.

papers.abstract: This study develops an inverse design framework for elastic metasurfaces with parametric polygonal pillars to manipulate transmitted flexural waves. The proposed unit cell is characterized by five geometric parameters, including three independently adjustable parameters defining its cross-sectional shape, allowing flexible control of the resonance characteristics. To address the increased complexity of identifying target modes with different polarizations, an automated modal screening procedure is introduced to construct a finite element dataset. The multilayer perceptron is trained as an efficient forward surrogate for predicting the characteristic frequencies of the target bending and compression modes. Based on the pretrained MLP, a tandem neural network enables on-demand retrieval of geometric parameters for prescribed resonance frequencies, while particle swarm optimization further explores alternative feasible configurations satisfying similar resonance conditions. Finally, phase gradient metasurfaces are constructed to demonstrate anomalous refraction, wave splitting, and self-bending flexural wave propagation through full-wave numerical simulations.

papers.title: Osteochondral unit–based management of focal articular cartilage and osteochondral defects: a narrative review of surgical repair, clinical decision-making, and tissue engineering
papers.abstract: The therapeutic goal for articular cartilage and osteochondral defects has increasingly emphasized osteochondral unit reconstruction. This review uses the principal osteochondral tissues targeted by each strategy as a framework to compare marrow stimulation, scaffold enhancement, osteochondral transplantation (autograft or allograft), cell-mediated regeneration, and engineered regeneration strategies in terms of their indications, clinical outcomes, limitations, and translational boundaries. A structured narrative synthesis was performed after searching PubMed and screening clinical studies, systematic reviews, and representative translational and preclinical studies; 127 references were ultimately included. Current evidence indicates that procedure selection is primarily informed by defect size and depth, subchondral bone status, lesion location, prior surgical history, and joint mechanical environment. Microfracture may be used for small, contained defects with limited subchondral bone involvement, but the long-term durability of the repair tissue remains inadequate. Autologous Matrix-Induced Chondrogenesis (AMIC) can enhance the reparative environment after marrow stimulation, yet evidence heterogeneity remains substantial across lesions and techniques. Osteochondral Autograft Transplantation (OAT) is suitable for small-to-medium, well-defined osteochondral defects in patients with high functional demands, although it is limited by autologous donor-site availability. Osteochondral Allograft Transplantation (OCA) can provide single-stage structural reconstruction for medium-to-large lesions involving subchondral bone or after previous treatment failure, but still faces challenges in graft availability, osseous integration, graft failure, and reoperation burden. Autologous Chondrocyte Implantation/Matrix-induced autologous chondrocyte implantation (ACI/MACI) is more applicable to medium-to-large focal full-thickness chondral defects, provided that the subchondral bone is largely intact or can be reconstructed concomitantly; its long-term outcomes are constrained by patient selection, correction of joint mechanics, rehabilitation duration, and cost. Hydrogels, biphasic or multiphasic scaffolds, and 3D bioprinting enable stratified biomimetic reconstruction, yet clinical evidence lags behind basic research. Therefore, articular cartilage repair should be individualized according to the osteochondral tissues involved and the extent of involvement, with concomitant correction of malalignment, joint instability, and meniscal deficiency. Future research should use standardized outcomes, long-term follow-up, and high-quality comparative studies to clarify the true added value and clinical translatability of emerging strategies relative to established procedures.

papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting offers substantial potential for reconstructing the structural and biological complexity of skin, yet its regenerative performance and clinical translation are constrained by the challenge of concurrently realizing printability, structural stability, and tissue remodeling with hydrogel bioinks. Beyond polymer composition alone, we discuss how molecular features, crosslinking chemistry, and network architecture collectively determine bioink performance and regenerative function. Recent studies show that dynamic crosslinking, interpenetrating networks, and hybrid or nanocomposite designs can improve the balance between printability and post-print stability while also regulating transport, degradation, and cell–material interactions. Importantly, these material properties are not independent design targets; they are mechanistically linked to the ability of bioinks to modulate the wound microenvironment, support vascularization, and promote extracellular matrix reconstruction. Although emerging biofabrication strategies extend these functionalities, they impose stricter requirements for precise regulation of polymer rheology, crosslinking kinetics, and dynamic network adaptability. Despite rapid progress, translation to clinical use remains hindered by limited biological fidelity, poor reproducibility, and the lack of standardized manufacturing and regulatory criteria. We therefore propose that future bioink development should shift from empirical formulation toward predictive and adaptive polymer systems in which network design, biological function, and manufacturing requirements are considered simultaneously. This structure–property–function perspective provides a rational framework for developing next-generation polymer bioinks with improved regenerative efficacy and translational potential.

Although satisfactory bone healing and functional recovery were observed in this patient, further studies are required to establish the safety, reproducibility, and long-term effectiveness of this combined approach.

Patient demographics, operative parameters (time, blood loss), and hospital stay were recorded. Fracture healing time, Harris Hip Score (HHS), and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) were evaluated preoperatively and at the final follow-up, with VAS also assessed postoperatively. Complications were documented. Results The mean follow-up was 63.86 months (range, 24–120). During the follow-up period, three patients died due to advanced age, and two patients were lost to follow-up because of changes in contact information or failure to attend scheduled visits. Mean operative time was 176.32 ± 20.46 min, and mean blood loss was 358.93 ± 188.59 mL. All fractures united, with a mean healing time of 3.89 months. HHS improved significantly from 43.93 preoperatively to 90.32 at final follow-up ( P < 0.001), and VAS decreased from 4.11 ± 1.03 to 0.43 ± 0.50 ( P < 0.001). Postoperative DVT occurred in 7 patients (mean onset: 7.71 ± 1.11 days), including one case progressing to pulmonary embolism requiring an inferior vena cava filter; all were successfully managed with rivaroxaban. Prosthesis subsidence was observed in 5 patients, of whom 3 remained stable and were monitored, while 2 with delayed union underwent revision with distally fixed cementless stems. No other complications (infection, nonunion, implant failure, loosening, or osteolysis) were observed in the remaining patients. papers.title: Active Learning with Imperfect Labels: Optimal Labeler Assignment and Sample Selection
papers.abstract: Active learning (AL) is commonly used in applications where labeling data are expensive or time consuming. In practice, however, labels are often noisy because of varying labeler expertise and annotation uncertainty, especially for complex or ambiguous samples. Learning from such imperfectly labeled data can degrade classifier performance. We propose an AL framework that explicitly accounts for label noise by optimally assigning labelers and selecting samples to minimize labeling error. Our approach, which is called optimal labeler assignment and sampling (OLAS), uses a noise model that depends on both labeler accuracy and model uncertainty to guide these decisions. We develop two tractable optimization formulations: one for assigning samples to labelers to minimize worst-case noise and another for selecting samples while controlling overall label noise. Theoretical results provide closed-form solutions under mild conditions. Empirical evaluations on benchmark data sets and a real-world warranty claim classification problem show that OLAS achieves the highest or near-highest classification accuracy among existing AL strategies across most settings using only a single label per sample.

papers.title: Techno-economic optimization of a heat-pipe microreactor, part II: Multi-objective optimization analysis
papers.abstract: Heat-pipe microreactors (HPMRs) are compact and transportable nuclear power systems exhibiting inherent safety, well-suited for deployment in remote regions where access is limited and reliance on costly fossil fuels is prevalent. In prior work, we developed a design optimization framework that incorporates techno-economic considerations through surrogate modeling and reinforcement learning (RL)-based optimization, focusing solely on minimizing the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) by using a bottom-up cost estimation approach. In this study, we extend that framework to a multi-objective optimization that uses the Pareto Envelope Augmented with Reinforcement Learning (PEARL) algorithm. The objectives include minimizing both the rod-integrated peaking factor ( F Δ h ) and LCOE—subject to safety and operational constraints. We evaluate three cost scenarios: (1) a high-cost axial and drum reflectors, (2) a low-cost axial reflector, and (3) low-cost axial and drum reflectors. Our findings indicate that reducing the solid moderator radius, pin pitch, and drum coating angle—all while increasing the fuel height—effectively lowers F Δ h . Across all three scenarios, four key strategies consistently emerged for optimizing LCOE: (1) minimizing the axial reflector contribution when costly, (2) reducing control drum reliance, (3) substituting expensive tri-structural isotropic (TRISO) fuel with axial reflector material priced at the level of graphite, and (4) maximizing fuel burnup. While PEARL demonstrates promise in navigating trade-offs across diverse design scenarios, discrepancies between surrogate model predictions and full-order simulations can lead to infeasibility in some cases, particularly for fuel lifetime and shutdown margin. Therefore, this study should be understood as a surrogate-guided trade-off exploration study rather than an effort to identify exact Pareto-optimal solutions. Further improvements are anticipated through constraint relaxation and surrogate development, constituting an ongoing area of investigation.

papers.title: Physics-informed Bayesian optimization for quantitative high-resolution transmission electron microscopy
papers.abstract: Abstract Quantitative high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) provides an indispensable means to understand structure-property relationships in atomic dimensions. Successful quantification requires reliable retrieval of essential atomic structural information despite artifacts arising from practically unavoidable imaging imperfections. Experimental observation combined with model-based iterative image simulation has enabled broad applications in quantitative structural and chemical determination of objects spanning zero to three dimensions. However, the large number of parameters involved makes the current multi-step, user-supervised iterative approach highly time-consuming, restricting its use to small sample areas and experienced users. In this work, we implement and apply a physics-informed Bayesian optimization (BO) framework to advance HRTEM quantification toward full automation and large-field-of-view analysis. Unlike conventional optimization methods, our approach adopts a stepwise strategy that fully leverages BO’s strength in handling high-dimensional parameter spaces, while its probabilistic engine efficiently refines the parameter space for rapid quantification. Using a BaTiO 3 single crystal that contains heavy, medium, and light elements as a model system, we demonstrate that the three-dimensional crystal structure can be determined from a single HRTEM image with a three- to four-order-of-magnitude improvement in time efficiency. This approach opens new avenues for fast, automated quantification over larger sample volumes and, promisingly, for in-situ applications.

papers.title: Interpretable human-label-free deep learning for real-bogus classification with uncertainty quantification
papers.abstract: Time-domain surveys generate large numbers of transient candidates, making real-bogus classification a critical step in automated discovery pipelines. Obtaining reliable human-labeled training sets is costly, while community-provided labels can be noisy and survey-dependent. We aim to develop a real-bogus classification framework for point-like astrophysical transient detections against bogus survey detections, that can be trained without human-labeled data using physically motivated injected transients and bogus-dominated survey data, that remains robust under strong class contamination, and that provides well-calibrated and reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ) suitable for downstream decision-making. We combine simulated transient injections with a heavily contaminated survey class and train a dual-network model using an asymmetric co-teaching strategy for classes with different label-noise levels. We evaluate performance on a labeled benchmark subset and analyze the learned representation with latent-space visualization tools. For UQ, we compare standard approaches (Monte Carlo dropout and deep ensembles) and propose a low-cost hybrid strategy that exploits the dual-network setting to improve calibration. We further extend the evaluation to the light-curve domain to assess recovery of light-curve classes. The method achieves strong real-bogus performance on the labeled subset and remains stable under severe class contamination. It recovers transient light-curve classes with high fidelity, while single-source identification is fundamentally limited by intrinsic ambiguity in light-curve-derived labels. Our hybrid UQ approach achieves competitive calibration relative to substantially more expensive ensemble baselines. Latent-space analyses indicate that uncertainty aligns with the decision boundary and reveal that the model can identify subclasses within the bogus population. Our results show that injection-driven, weakly supervised training can enable scalable and consistent real-bogus classification without human-labeled training data while providing calibrated uncertainties. The methodology is well suited for transfer to forthcoming surveys by rerunning the injection-based training pipeline.

papers.title: Conformal uncertainty quantification for BayesAge epigenetic age predictions
papers.abstract: Abstract Epigenetic clocks predict chronological age from DNA methylation (DNAm) profiles, yet most provide point estimates without calibrated uncertainty. This limits their use when quantified error bounds are required. We apply conformal prediction to BayesAge, a maximum-likelihood clock that models nonlinear DNAm–age relationships using a small set of CpG loci and a count-based likelihood. Split conformal prediction yields distribution-free prediction intervals with finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees under exchangeability and requires only a single model fit per split. We also evaluate a locally scaled variant that produces age-dependent interval widths using a locally estimated error scale. In our targeted bisulfite sequencing cohort, split conformalized BayesAge attains near-nominal empirical coverage while preserving BayesAge point-prediction accuracy. The locally scaled variant yields wider intervals at older ages, but its coverage is less stable in small-calibration regimes, consistent with additional uncertainty from estimating the local scale. Relative to Monte Carlo intervals that propagate read-sampling variability and to higher-dimensional linear baselines (conformalized linear quantile regression and conformalized Lasso regression), conformalized BayesAge provides calibrated uncertainty using substantially fewer CpG sites and with weaker age-dependent structure in residuals. These results support conformal prediction as a practical approach for uncertainty quantification in DNAm-based age estimation.

papers.title: Where Individual-Effect Information Survives: A Diagnostic Ladder for World Models
papers.abstract: World models are widely used for planning and control, but it remains unclear whether they can answer counterfactual questions of the form “what would have happened to this individual under a different action.” Such a question sits at the third rung of Pearl’s ladder and requires abduction, inferring from the history what distinguishes this individual from the others. This paper makes two things measurable, whether abduction is worth performing in an environment and where a trained model loses its answer. The abducible share is the share of the variance of the individual treatment effect that the history reveals and the branch-point observation does not. It comes with an explicit estimation floor below which no value of it is interpretable. Six of our twelve environments cannot support the measurement, since each fails one of five conditions we state on the environment and the estimator, and the parameterisation of the estimand alone takes the abducible share from 0.06 to 0.79. We propose reporting the abducible share as a certificate carrying its floor and its settings, and the calibration of a model as a certificate of calibration slope, order and error. Substituting a trained model’s own quantities into the same decomposition locates where the individual effect is lost. In a reservoir computer, the latent state of a recurrent state-space model (RSSM) retains 0.195 of an abducible share of 0.213, whereas its imagination rollout returns 0.125. In a two-qubit processor the imagined state keeps this information over twenty imagined steps while the decoded output loses it, which places the loss on the output side of the rollout.

papers.title: An empirical evaluation of first-order Noisy Input Gaussian Process Regression under increasing input uncertainty
papers.abstract: Gaussian Process (GP) regression provides a flexible probabilistic framework for learning non-linear input–output relationships, but standard formulations typically assume that input variables are observed without error. Noisy Input Gaussian Process Regression (NIGP) addresses this limitation by propagating input uncertainty through a first-order Taylor approximation of the GP posterior mean, thereby introducing an input-dependent effective variance. This study presents a systematic empirical evaluation of the established first-order NIGP formulation under progressively increasing input uncertainty rather than proposing a new mathematical correction. Synthetic experiments were conducted using a sine–trend function with input-noise standard deviations ranging from 0.1 to 1.0 and 50 paired Monte Carlo replicates per condition. Performance was assessed using Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Negative Log Predictive Density (NLPD), Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP), absolute coverage error (ACE), mean prediction interval width (MPIW), Winkler score, and Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS). The first-order approximation was additionally evaluated against Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation and a second-order Taylor reference, while further experiments examined multiple non-linear benchmarks, heterogeneous input uncertainty, and multidimensional correlated input noise. In the principal experiment, GP and NIGP exhibited similar point-prediction performance at low input-noise levels, whereas NIGP produced substantially lower RMSE and MAE from σ x = 0.4 onward, with the largest differences occurring at high noise levels. At σ x = 1.0, mean RMSE decreased from 2.10461 for GP to 0.35937 for NIGP, while mean MAE decreased from 1.59203 to 0.29728. The corresponding bias–variance analysis showed that these improvements were associated with reductions in both predictive bias and variance. Probabilistic performance was noise-dependent: the models were broadly similar at low noise levels, while NIGP produced substantially narrower intervals and lower NLPD, Winkler, and CRPS values at higher noise levels. However, its coverage relative to the nominal 95% level was not uniformly improved. The first-order approximation also deteriorated as input noise increased, with mean relative error rising from approximately 2.1% at σ x = 0.1 to 75.8% at σ x = 1.0, while empirical convergence of the iterative procedure declined from 100% to 34%. The results demonstrate that the empirical benefits of NIGP become increasingly evident under moderate-to-high input uncertainty, but its effectiveness remains constrained by the accuracy of the first-order approximation and the numerical stability of the iterative uncertainty-propagation procedure.

papers.title: New Non-Destructive Surface Roughness Inspection of Additively Manufactured Metallic Parts Using Scanning Acoustic Microscopy
papers.abstract: Although additive manufacturing enables the production of metallic components with complex geometries, accurately characterizing their surfaces remains challenging, especially in regions beyond the reach of conventional techniques. To address this challenge, this study investigates scanning acoustic microscopy (SAM) as an automated, non-destructive method for measuring the surface roughness of stainless steel 316L cubes fabricated by selective laser melting. A dedicated image-processing pipeline was developed to detect the water–specimen interface in SAM B-scan images using robust surface echo tracking and convert it into a calibrated surface profile. ISO-based spatial filtering was then applied to separate roughness from measurement noise, waviness, and surface form, enabling the calculation of different surface roughness parameters. To evaluate the proposed method, Ra was selected for validation using seven reference standards with nominal values ranging from 0.8 to 50μm. The influence of Gaussian filtering was also investigated by comparing two formulations. SAM successfully distinguished all seven roughness levels, with absolute deviations ranging from 0.327 to 1.772μm for the cutoff-matched formulation and from 0.199 to 4.075μm for the simplified formulation. Furthermore, repeatability measurements demonstrated mean coefficients of variation below 2% across all investigated specimens. Comparison between the proposed SAM pipeline, digital and laser confocal microscopes showed mean absolute deviations of 0.75, 1.30, and 2.85μm, respectively, from shared reference values. Building on this comparison, the optical instruments were used to assess SAM measurements on fabricated cubes without known reference values. Overall, the findings support SAM as a complementary method for quantitative surface roughness evaluation.

papers.title: Reorienting School Mathematics Learning: Integrating Active, Differentiated, and Technology-Enhanced Instruction
papers.abstract: Scientific and technological developments highlight the need for school mathematics instruction that responds to students’ diverse characteristics and learning needs. This study synthesized concepts and research findings concerning the integration of active learning, differentiated instruction, and digital technology in mathematics education. A systematic literature review examined ten relevant scientific articles published between 2020 and 2026. Findings were analyzed thematically through identification, classification, comparison, and synthesis. The reviewed literature indicated that active learning supports students’ engagement in constructing understanding and developing mathematical thinking. Differentiated instruction accommodates variations in readiness, interests, abilities, and learning needs, while digital technology facilitates access to interactive, flexible, and adaptive learning resources. Their integration has the potential to support meaningful, inclusive, participatory, and responsive mathematics instruction. The study contributes an integrative pedagogical perspective that positions active learning, differentiation, and technology as complementary dimensions of instructional design. Further research should develop and empirically test integrated instructional models across educational levels, examining their implications for conceptual understanding, mathematical reasoning, problem-solving skills, motivation, and learning autonomy.

papers.title: Examining the patient- and system-related forces influencing the responsiveness of hip fracture care in Zimbabwe: Findings from an ethnographic study
papers.abstract: Rapidly rising longevity and the projected increase in fractures among older adults in Southern Africa underscores the necessity to strengthen healthcare systems in the region. Delivering orthopaedic care to older people within a multi-disciplinary framework is widely recommended. This ethnographic study sought to examine the responsiveness of hip fracture care in Zimbabwe and the influence of patient- and system-related forces We used ethnographic methods to examine the experiences of patients and caregivers and characterise hip fracture care provision. Case studies were undertaken with 40 patients (22 male, 18 female) and 33 caregivers (6 male, 27 female), including family members and friends. These data were complemented by interviews and observations of clinical practice with 42 healthcare professionals (23 female, 19 male) involved in the delivery of hip fracture services, including orthopaedic surgeons, physicians and physiotherapists. Participants were purposively sampled from six hospitals providing hip fracture care across Northern Zimbabwe. Snowball sampling was also used to recruit additional study participants. Data were analysed using an abductive analytical approach. Patients’ and caregivers’ experiences revealed lengthy hospital stays, poor communication concerning diagnosis and treatment, undignified continence management, and limited access to social support. Patients’ experiences highlighted the importance of access to pain relief medication, and the impact of unaffordable care – elements distinct from those within current responsiveness frameworks. Health professionals explained how resource constraints, understaffing, and changes in pain management processes impacted their ability to meet patients’ needs. Yet, their narratives told of the various actions they employed to circumvent health system constraints and respond to patient priorities. Considering these findings, we highlight key considerations for health systems responsiveness, including considering the role of socioeconomic factors. We also propose practical recommendations for improving responsive hip fracture care in Zimbabwe, such as developing guidelines for patient optimisation and standardisation of hip implant costs.

papers.abstract: An artificial neural network (ANN)-based digital twin feed controller, aiming to optimise bioprocess performance, was implemented in fed-batch bioprocesses of Lactobacillus rhamnosus LRH30 for the production of biomass. The online data from several fed-batch bioprocesses in dairy-based cultivations with L. rhamnosus were utilised to develop an ANN that predicts the biomass and growth rate of L. rhamnosus in the process. This growth rate estimator was first validated through unit testing before being applied in model predictive control to select the best control action to drive feed addition to the process. The controller was implemented in fed-batch bioprocesses and the growth rate was estimated in real time, leading to the highest cell dry weight biomass concentrations obtained for L. rhamnosus LRH30 of 36.23 g/L in this study, with growth-rate overshoot and increased feed addition also contributing to the biomass accumulation despite imperfect setpoint tracking. The dose-dependent effect of L. rhamnosus LRH30 samples on cytokine secretion from murine macrophages was further explored, and an anti-inflammatory effect was found at a dosage of 10 mg/mL of bacterial cell dry weight. These experiments demonstrate the first steps in the implementation phase that will ultimately lead to a better controlled bioprocess with higher yields of L. rhamnosus biomass. Future research will focus on the continuous development of the ANN through the incorporation of more datasets, while simultaneously exploring the functional potential of L. rhamnosus LRH30.

papers.title: Teaching Intelligent Fluid Dynamics through Engineering Cases: Design and Preliminary Practice of a Graduate Teaching Case Library
papers.abstract: Effective integration of classroom instruction and research practice is essential to the quality of graduate engineering education. To address three persistent weaknesses in the teaching of fluid dynamics simulation courses, a graduate teaching case library, Intelligent Fluid Dynamics, was established. Specifically, theoretical instruction is delivered in isolation from research practice, systematic training in the application of acquired knowledge is absent, and assessment fails to reflect the stated course objectives. The reform takes the CFD simulation skills already acquired by students as its point of departure and targets research competence in intelligent fluid dynamics. Two complete teaching cases are under development: physics-informed neural network (PINN)-based flow field reconstruction and inversion, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based active flow control of airfoils. Each case is supported by a knowledge-to-competence map and an instructor-oriented teaching guide. Learning is organized as a three-level progression, applied foundations, specialized depth and innovative practice, and is supported by purpose-built teaching procedures and an assessment scheme combining coursework with a final examination. Preliminary results indicate improved transfer of prior learning and enhanced specialized competence, and the experience is expected to be informative for comparable graduate courses.

papers.title: Crop biophysical parameter estimation via AI-enhanced hyperspectral remote sensing
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral remote sensing has become a key approach for retrieving crop parameters related to canopy structure, physiological status, biochemical composition and productivity. However, many current methods remain centered on task-specific empirical fitting between spectral features and target parameters. Their transferability is limited when crop growth varies across phenological stages, observation scales, sensor conditions and planting systems. Hyperspectral crop-parameter retrieval is moving toward an intelligent inversion paradigm, which is jointly supported by spatio-temporal-spectral representation, mechanistic constraints and trustworthy decision-making. Accordingly, we synthesize recent progress in crop spectral-response mechanisms, satellite-airborne-ground coordinated observation, spatio-temporal consistency processing, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven retrieval models and mechanism-data fusion. Particular attention is given to the integration of hyperspectral features with crop-growth processes and canopy radiative transfer. We also examine transferable spatio-temporal-spectral representations, applicability-domain assessment and uncertainty quantification. Future advances should move beyond improving the accuracy of multi-spatio-temporal observations and instead progress toward mechanism-informed intelligent retrieval that integrates crop-growth knowledge with deep learning. This approach should explicitly represent crop growth processes, spatial heterogeneity and applicability constraints, thereby supporting more reliable crop monitoring, growth diagnosis, yield prediction and decision-making in complex agricultural systems.

papers.abstract: The kinetics of phase-structural transformations and the complex local mechanical response of the surface layers of Ti–6Al–4V titanium alloy manufactured by selective laser melting (SLM) were investigated during diffusion nitriding in a commercially pure nitrogen environment. Gas nitriding was performed in three isothermal regimes (750°C, 800°C, 850°C) with holding times of 5, 10, and 15 h. Quantitative X-ray diffraction analysis showed that at 850°C for 15 h, the total volume fraction of nitride phases exceeded 61%, with textured tetragonal nitride ε-Ti2N (50.21%) being the dominant phase. Using the instrumental microindentation method according to the Oliver–Farr algorithms (under a load of 0.5 N), a monotonic increase in the mechanical characteristics of the modified surface was observed. The maximum strengthening was obtained at 850°C, 15 h: the microhardness HIT increased in 2.7 times compared to the initial state (from 4.99 to 13.44 GPa), and the elastic modulus EIT reached 205.33 GPa. Analysis of the load-unload curves showed a regular redistribution of the energy components of the deformation contact: the work of plastic deformation Wplast decreased by 37% (to 0.212 mkJ), and the elastic recovery coefficient ηIT increased to 33.95%. In combination with the calculated nine-fold increase in the resistance to plastic deformation H3/Е2 to 0.0574 GPa, this justifies the high ability of the formed gradient structure to elastically relax contact forces without the risk of microcracking and tribodestruction of the nitride layer.

papers.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Stability Prediction and Shelf-Life Estimation of Pharmaceutical Formulations
papers.abstract: Stability testing determines whether a pharmaceutical product keeps its identity, strength, quality and purity over its labeled shelf life, but conventional studies are slow, expensive and material-intensive, and they offer limited insight into why a formulation degrades. Artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning (ML) in particular, is increasingly used to predict degradation pathways, physical stability, and time to specification failure from formulation, process, structural and early stability data. This review summarizes the scientific and regulatory background of stability assessment; the main AI methods applied (tree ensembles, kernel methods, Gaussian processes, deep and graph neural networks, and hybrid mechanistic-ML models); data requirements and feature engineering; applications to small molecules, amorphous solid dispersions, biologics, nucleic acids and drug-delivery systems; and an end-to-end workflow for AI-assisted shelf-life estimation. We discuss validation, uncertainty quantification, explainability and regulatory expectations, and outline the challenges that must be solved before AI-derived predictions can support labeled shelf-life claims. Current evidence suggests that AI is best positioned today as a decision-support tool for formulation screening, study design and risk assessment, complementing rather than replacing real-time stability data.

papers.abstract: Abstract The potential of electric vehicles (EVs) as an important flexible resource in the electricity market is increasingly prominent, but existing dispatch strategies often overlook the coordination mechanism between distribution network physical constraints and multilevel market signals. To address this issue, this paper aims to develop a real-time intelligent charging optimization strategy for EV-grid collaboration to balance the profits of charging operators, the preferences of vehicle owners, and grid safety. This paper integrates model predictive control (MPC) and dynamic programming (DP) to construct an MPC local control + DP global planning framework for multiperiod charging and discharging optimization, and designs four integrated scheduling strategies based on the EV2Gym platform. The main novel contributions of this study are twofold: first, a three-level price linkage model is designed to clarify the interaction rules between the regional day-ahead market and the local real-time market; second, grid factors such as transformer power limits and photovoltaic accommodation constraints are quantitatively integrated into the optimization framework. Experiments demonstrate that compared with existing technologies, the proposed strategy increases profits by 8%, decreases the risk of transformer overload by 15%, and improves the PV accommodation rate by 20%, while successfully controlling battery degradation within an acceptable range. This study provides an effective and practical solution for the implementation of large-scale intelligent charging.
