papers.title: A physics-informed neural network approach for surrogate modeling for PWRs LOOP events
papers.abstract: Accurate and rapid predictions of reactor transients such as Loss of Offsite Power (LOOP) events in Pressurized Water Reactors (PWRs) is critical for reactor safety assessment. Traditional highly benchmarked codes are computationally expensive, prohibiting their direct use in fast safety assessments. To address these challenges, this study investigates the potential of physics learning based surrogate models. We developed and compared data-driven and physics-informed surrogate models for predicting transient thermal-hydraulics in a triple-loop PWR under the LOOP conditions, focusing on the evolution of primary system pressure, fuel temperature and coolant temperature. Four data-driven Deep Neural Network (DNN) architectures and three Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) variants were trained using data sets covering 36 transient scenarios. Each scenario was varied with initial reactor condition, system configuration and boundary constraints. The results show that the improved Multi-Layer Perceptron (best data driven model) achieved an R 2 of 0.7015 for primary coolant temperature ( T c ), 0.6701 for fuel temperature ( T f ) and 0.8364 for primary system pressure ( P p ) on held-out test scenarios. The Shared-encoder Multi-Head PINN improved R 2 to 0.7449 for T c , 0.6987 for T f and 0.8519 for P p . The PINN also demonstrated improved robustness to sensor measurement uncertainty, with an MAPE increase of 0.1274% under 3% Gaussian input noise, compared to 0.2954% for the DNN. The study also shows incorporating governing heat and pressure equations within the learning process improves the predictive performance on held-out scenario trajectories within the training envelope, which indicates that while PINNs offer a promising path to physical consistency, the fidelity of the underlying governing equations is paramount to achieve physically consistent predictions. This finding highlights the need for a balance between data-driven learning and physical constraints.

papers.title: Game-Based Teaching in Medical Education:An Experimental Assessment of Students’ Satisfaction
papers.abstract: Background: Medical learning is a complicated phenomenon which involves critical thinking and problem-solving ability. To make the medical subjects interesting, it's important to try out implementation of an innovative and interesting method for teaching and learning. Game-based or quiz-based learning is a challenging learning tool that promote active learning and team participation and it provides a better learning environment. The aim of this study was to assess medical students’ satisfaction using game-based teaching method which may provide insights for better learning environment. Materials and methods: This experimental study was conducted in the Department of Physiology, Chittagong Medical College and Institute of Applied Health Science, Chattogram during the period from January to December 2024. Total 126 apparently healthy 1st year medical students were included in this study by stratified random sampling. All students were undergone a pre-intervention test to measure their baseline knowledge on the chosen content. Then they were randomly allocated into experimental and control groups by lottery method. Traditional Lecture-Based Learning (TLBL) was used for teaching in the control group and Game-Based Learning (GBL) method was used in the experimental group. Just after implementing two teaching methods, a post-intervention test was done in both groups to measure their knowledge achievement. A retention test and a satisfaction survey was arranged after two weeks to assess the students’ retention of knowledge and satisfaction, in which 59 students in experimental group and 63 students in control group participated. Students in both groups were given a questionnaire to measure their satisfaction. Differences in satisfaction score and satisfaction level between two groups was assessed using unpaired t-tests and χ2 test, respectively. Result: In this study, mean value of satisfaction score was significantly higher in the experimental group than the control group (p≤0.05). Majority of the students in experimental group replied with strongly agreed while a poor percentage of the students in control group replied with strongly agreed (p≤0.001) regarding their teaching technique. Conclusion: The result of this study suggested that game-based teaching-learning was well liked and accepted by students as a more satisfying teaching method. papers.title: Superior directional thermal conductivity and stiffness in rectangular γ-graphyne revealed by neuroevolution machine-learning potentials
papers.abstract: Graphynes have emerged as promising carbon allotropes for next-generation nanoelectronics and thermoelectric devices due to their unique combination of porous frameworks, tunable bandgaps, and unconventional thermal transport. In this work we comprehensively investigate the thermal, vibrational, and mechanical properties of hexagonal ( γ -GY) and rectangular (r γ -GY) graphynes by developing an accurate and efficient machine-learning interatomic potential trained via an active learning framework. The developed neuroevolution potential closely captures the potential energy surfaces of both structures, showing excellent agreement with reference first-principles calculations. Molecular dynamics simulations driven by this potential reveal a remarkable directional anisotropy in the rectangular phase. Notably, the zigzag direction exhibits a significantly enhanced thermal performance compared to both its armchair direction and the hexagonal counterpart. This superior thermal conductivity is accompanied by higher lattice stiffness, higher phonon group velocities, and a substantially larger contribution from long-wavelength phonons with extended effective mean free paths. Spectral and modal decompositions reveal the dominance of low-frequency modes, where in-plane branches dominate the zigzag direction of both structures, whereas out-of-plane modes slightly surpass in-plane thermal channels along the rectangular armchair axis. These findings provide insights into how lattice topology and acetylenic groups influence phonon transport, contributing to a better understanding of directional thermal transport in graphyne-based nanostructures. • Neuroevolution potentials are developed for hexagonal and rectangular γ -graphynes. • Strong thermal and mechanical anisotropy is observed in r γ -graphyne. • The rectangular phase has superior thermal conductivity along the zigzag direction. • Thermal conductivity anisotropy correlates with lattice mechanical anisotropy.

papers.title: An efficient ensemble deep learning model for lung cancer classification from histopathological images
papers.abstract: Globally, lung cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer and the primary reason for cancer-related mortality. Early cancer detection increases the chances of successful treatments, thereby reducing patient mortality rates. Recently, medical imaging has been the most reliable technique to assist in diagnosing lung cancer and monitoring its treatment. Moreover, standard image classification tools often fall short in automatically identifying cancer, slowing down diagnoses. Therefore, automated systems for early lung cancer detection must be developed for greater sensitivity and accuracy. The emergence of deep learning techniques has enabled faster, more effective diagnosis and classification of lung nodules in the medical imaging field. Therefore, this article proposes an Ensemble Deep Learning Model for Lung Cancer Classification (EDLM-LCC) based on Medical Imaging. The proposed model aims to accurately classify lung cancer into adenocarcinoma, benign, and squamous cell carcinoma categories using advanced image analysis techniques. To accomplish this, the presented technique utilizes Non-Local Means filtering for image denoising. In addition, the EDLM-LCC system employs Convolutional Block Attention Module-ResNet50 as the feature extraction to obtain deep and discriminative feature representations from preprocessed images. For classification, an ensemble of Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, Temporal Convolutional Network, and Gated Recurrent Unit is adopted using a weighted majority voting strategy to improve robustness and classification accuracy. To enhance the performance of the presented method, the parameter selection process takes place using Bayesian optimization. The experimental evaluation of the presented EDLM-LCC system is carried out using a benchmark lung cancer histopathological images dataset, and the results indicate that the model demonstrates outstanding classification performance with an accuracy of 96.67% compared to existing techniques.

papers.title: Optimized Operating Strategy for the Thermal Management of a Battery Electric City Bus Using Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Electrified propulsion systems offer the potential to reduce global CO2 emissions in the transportation sector, particularly in the field of urban mobility. Electric city buses combine the benefits of public transport systems with locally emission-free mobility. To ensure sufficient range for daily duty cycles, energy efficiency is crucial. Thermal management has a significant impact on the energy demand of battery electric vehicles. Therefore, efficiency can be improved by employing an integrated thermal management architecture that interconnects the individual coolant circuits and enables system-wide optimization. This study proposes an approach to optimize the operating strategy for the thermal management of a battery electric city bus. The important thermal components, including the drive system, battery system and HVAC system, are investigated. Experiments were carried out using a test setup of the system to identify the thermal behavior of the components. The study develops a simulation model of the thermal system of a BEV bus and subsequently uses this model to optimize the operating strategy by means of Bayesian optimization. The goal is to minimize energy demand under representative driving and environmental conditions in the city of Hamburg. The simulation-based analyses highlight potential gains resulting from the optimization of coolant temperatures and the flow rates of the components. Finally, a route- and temperature-based operating strategy is recommended.

papers.title: Interpretable Landslide Susceptibility Mapping in Pacitan, Indonesia Using Bayesian-Optimized XGBoost and SHAP Analysis
papers.abstract: Background: Landslide susceptibility mapping is essential in areas with complex topographic and geological conditions, such as Pacitan Regency, Indonesia, to identify landslide-prone areas and assess the factors influencing landslide susceptibility. Objective: This study developed a landslide susceptibility mapping model using Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), optimized through Bayesian optimization and interpreted using the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method. Methods: The dataset consisted of 1,486 samples, comprising 743 landslide occurrence points and 743 non-landslide points. Eleven landslide conditioning factors were used as predictor variables: elevation, aspect, slope, geology, land use, profile curvature, plan curvature, distance to roads, distance to rivers, Stream Power Index (SPI), and Topographic Wetness Index (TWI). Model hyperparameter optimization was performed using Bayesian optimization with a Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE). Results: The optimized XGBoost model achieved an accuracy of 69.80%, a precision of 70.34%, a recall of 68.46%, an F1 score of 69.39%, and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.7564 on the independent test set. The resulting susceptibility map classified the study area into five categories: very low, low, moderate, high, and very high susceptibility. SHAP analysis identified slope, aspect, plan curvature, geology, and distance to roads as the dominant factors influencing model predictions. Conclusion: Integrating Bayesian optimization, XGBoost, and SHAP provides an interpretable approach to landslide susceptibility mapping in Pacitan Regency. The resulting susceptibility map and feature-level explanations can support preliminary disaster risk assessment and spatial planning. However, residual classification errors and limitations associated with the use of static environmental predictors should be considered when interpreting the results.

papers.title: The Influence of Workshop Format on the Enhancement of Financial Literacy for Public Pre-Retiree Employees at Arusha City Council
papers.abstract: This study examined the influence of retirement planning workshops on enhancing financial literacy among public pre-retiree employees at Arusha City Council. Specifically, the study evaluated the influence of workshop content, assessed the impact of workshop duration, and examined the influence of workshop format on financial literacy. The study adopted a pragmatic research philosophy and a mixed-methods approach using a descriptive research design. The target population comprised 129 pre-retiree employees, workshop facilitators, human resource officers, and financial advisors, from which a sample of 98 respondents was determined. Data were collected using questionnaires, interviews, and documentary review. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis, while qualitative data were analysed thematically. Of the 98 questionnaires distributed, 95 were returned and analysed. The findings revealed that workshop content had a mixed influence on financial literacy. Although 31.6% of respondents agreed that workshop content helped them manage budgets and control expenses, 34.7% disagreed or strongly disagreed, indicating inadequacies in practical and personalised financial guidance. Workshop duration was found to be an important factor, with 44.2% of respondents agreeing that the duration was sufficient for understanding basic budgeting techniques, while a substantial proportion indicated that more time was required to address complex investment topics. Workshop format was also important, with 52.6% of respondents preferring active learning methods such as group discussions and hands-on exercises, followed by 26.3% who preferred offline, face-to-face workshops. Only 5.3% preferred online learning formats. Multiple regression analysis demonstrated that workshop duration had the strongest positive and statistically significant influence on financial literacy (β = 0.628, p < 0.001), followed by workshop format (β = 0.421, p < 0.001). Workshop content had a statistically significant but negative relationship with financial literacy (β = -0.117, p = 0.036), suggesting that the existing content required improvement in relevance, practical application, and personalisation. Collectively, workshop content, duration, and format explained 85.8% of the variation in financial literacy (R² = 0.858; F = 181.889, p < 0.001). The study concludes that effective retirement planning workshops should allocate sufficient time to complex financial topics, prioritise interactive and participatory learning, and redesign content to provide practical and personalised financial guidance. The study recommends continuous follow-up support and differentiated workshop sessions to address the diverse financial needs of public pre-retiree employees.

papers.title: Optimization of power allocation scheduling and component sizing in battery-assisted electrolyser systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a co-design optimization framework for battery-assisted electrolyser systems aimed at improving the cost-effectiveness of green hydrogen production. As renewable energy sources (RES) increasingly strain electricity grids, decentralized power-to-hydrogen (P2H) production can mitigate grid imbalance while supplying a clean energy carrier, yet its financial viability remains uncertain. The proposed framework integrates models of battery energy storage systems (BESS), electrolysers, RES, and grid connections, and optimizes them on two levels: Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) determines the operational strategy that maximizes operating profit, while Bayesian Optimization (BO) selects the component sizing that maximizes net present value (NPV) over a continuous three-year horizon. The framework is applied to two real-world cases: a grid-limited 2 MW solar site (case A) and a more balanced solar–wind site (case B). For case A the optimal design pairs a 964 kW electrolyser with a 220 kWh battery, whereas case B favors a 475 kW electrolyser without a battery, showing that battery storage is decisive only when the grid connection is small. At a hydrogen price of €8/kg both systems are near break-even (NPV €−0.1 to €−0.9 million) and become clearly profitable at €16/kg (NPV €3.9–4.3 million); a sensitivity analysis shows they remain firmly loss-making across the €3–5/kg range projected for 2030. The electrolyser operates with an average efficiency of about 80% (HHV), at a levelized cost of hydrogen of about €10/kg. These results quantify how hydrogen price, grid capacity, and component sizing jointly govern the techno-economic feasibility of P2H systems, and provide a transferable framework for their cost-effective design.

papers.title: STUDENTS’ PERCEPTIONS OF DIGITAL OUTCOME TASKS USING BOOK CREATOR IN AN INTERNATIONAL EFL CLASSROOM
papers.abstract: Several prior studies have primarily examined teachers' perceptions regarding digital multimedia effectiveness through the Book Creator platform. However, how learners perceive specific digital outcome tasks using Book Creator within English language learning frameworks remains underexplored. Under an Outcome-Based Education (OBE) framework, the instructional process prioritizes measurable learning competencies demonstrated through authentic student performances. This study aimed to investigate English as a Foreign Language (EFL) students' perceptions of digital outcome tasks using Book Creator within an OBE curriculum. This qualitative descriptive study involved 19 international class students enrolled in an Active English course who completed digital book projects. Thematic analysis revealed that integrating Book Creator strengthened students' academic responsibility, digital literacy, intrinsic motivation, and active learning engagement, although learners encountered technical limitations and time management constraints. ABSTRAK Beberapa penelitian sebelumnya telah mengkaji persepsi pengajar terhadap efektivitas multimedia digital melalui platform Book Creator. Namun, kajian mengenai persepsi siswa terhadap penugasan luaran digital (digital outcome tasks) berbasis Book Creator dalam kerangka pembelajaran bahasa Inggris masih sangat terbatas. Dalam kerangka Outcome-Based Education (OBE), proses pembelajaran menitikberatkan pada pencapaian kompetensi terukur melalui unjuk kerja autentik siswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis persepsi siswa English as a Foreign Language (EFL) terhadap implementasi tugas luaran digital menggunakan Book Creator dalam kerangka OBE. Penelitian kualitatif deskriptif ini melibatkan 19 mahasiswa kelas internasional pada mata kuliah Active English yang menyelesaikan proyek pembuatan buku digital. Hasil analisis tematik menunjukkan bahwa integrasi Book Creator berhasil memperkuat tanggung jawab akademik, literasi digital, motivasi intrinsik, serta keterlibatan aktif siswa, meskipun mereka menghadapi kendala manajemen waktu dan keterbatasan fitur teknis aplikasi.

papers.title: Dual Physics-Informed Neural Networks Based on Traveling- Wave Decomposition for Boundary Reflection Solutions of Wave Equations
papers.abstract: We propose a dual physics-informed neural network (Dual-PINN) for wave equations by incorporating the characteristic structure of the one-dimensional d’Alembert solution. Two neural branches are associated with the characteristic coordinates x−ct and x+ct to represent counter-propagating wave components, and their outputs are jointly constrained by the governing equation and auxiliary conditions. Homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries can be imposed exactly through a trial function. For one-dimensional problems, an approximation result shows that the dual-branch representation can approximate solutions of the form u(x,t)=F(x−ct)+G(x+ct) arbitrarily well under standard universal-approximation assumptions, without implying convergence of the non-convex training procedure. Numerical examples involving periodic propagation, boundary reflection, and a two-dimensional wave problem show that the proposed representation captures the tested wave dynamics effectively. The two-dimensional case is treated as an empirical extension, suggesting the potential of characteristic-informed neural representations for wave-equation modeling.

papers.title: Dual-Adaptive Preview Model Predictive Control for Path Tracking of Differential-Drive Tracked Vehicles
papers.abstract: This study addresses the challenges of coordinating tracking accuracy and steering control stability in agricultural differential-drive tracked vehicles, particularly their adaptability to varying working conditions. An adaptive preview Model Predictive Control (MPC) path-tracking algorithm is developed using an electronically controlled modified differential-drive tracked vehicle as the test platform. A preview MPC controller is constructed based on kinematic analysis and a vehicle preview tracking error model, with a fuzzy controller optimizing the objective function’s weight matrix. A speed- and path-dependent preview-distance selection criterion is formulated, and an improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) provides an optional numerical implementation of preview-distance selection. The corresponding fixed-state objective admits a closed-form analytical solution. A tracked vehicle model was built based on a Robot Operating System (ROS), and a path tracking controller was built based on Simulink. Simulations and field tests at 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 m/s evaluate lateral tracking error and steering angular-velocity statistics against separate fixed-preview baselines. Relative to the 3.0 m baseline, mean absolute lateral error decreases by 30.13–56.00% in simulation and 46.05–72.57% in field tests. Relative to the 1.0 m baseline, lateral-error changes depend on speed, while angular-velocity standard deviation decreases by 22.23–40.67% in simulation and 24.10–46.39% in field tests. These results characterize the tested controller configurations and show a condition-dependent trade-off between lateral error and steering-response variability.

papers.title: Deep reinforcement learning–driven model-based adaptive PID strategy for six-wheeled rocker–bogie mobile platform
papers.abstract: Introduction Six-wheel rocker–bogie rovers encounter nonlinear dynamics, variable traction, and wheel slip that can degrade the performance of fixed-gain proportional–integral–derivative (PID) controllers. This study develops a hybrid deep reinforcement learning–PID framework to improve steering and drive control under these conditions. Methods Two Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) actor–critic agents adapt the steering and drive PID gains online using low-level dynamic feedback. The reward functions penalise tracking errors, wheel slip, inter-joint mismatch, and abrupt control variations. The framework was evaluated in a three-dimensional MATLAB Simscape Multibody environment incorporating suspension articulation, wheel–terrain contact, and load redistribution. Comparisons with conventional PID and standard DDPG-PID controllers examined tracking accuracy, learning convergence, actuator responses, and disturbance rejection. Results The proposed framework demonstrated more consistent learning convergence, reduced tracking deviations, and smoother actuator torque responses than the baseline controllers. Online gain adaptation improved the steering and drive responses under simulated variations in traction, slip, and payload distribution. The shaped rewards reduced fluctuations in gain updates and critic estimates. Discussion These simulation findings support the potential of reinforcement learning–based PID gain adaptation for low-level control of rocker–bogie rovers under uncertain operating conditions. The framework retains the conventional PID structure while introducing data-driven adaptation. Hardware-in-the-loop testing and physical rover experiments remain necessary to establish performance beyond simulation.

papers.abstract: The integration of renewable energy into buildings constitutes a major challenge for Home Energy Management Systems (HEMS) due to various uncertainties in demand, grid generation, and energy prices. In this paper, we formulate the HEMS control problem as a Markov Decision Process and introduce a simulation-based framework that combines Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with Bayesian Neural Networks (BNN) for uncertainty-aware decision-making. By using Monte Carlo dropout, our PPO-BNN approach explicitly captures epistemic uncertainty to optimize battery charging and discharging in a building simulation environment. Compared to standard PPO, our approach demonstrates superior performance, achieving a 52.1% reduction in deep-discharge events and a 14.3% improvement in annualized net economic value. These results underscore the critical role of Bayesian uncertainty quantification in developing robust, efficient, and sustainable control strategies for building energy simulation and performance optimization.

papers.abstract: This study addresses the slow convergence, limited representation of local high-gradient regions, and accumulation of boundary errors encountered by conventional physics-informed neural networks in predicting unsteady flow-fields around subsea pipelines. A RANS-GPINN model based on the RANS governing equations and integrating a residual-gradient enhancement mechanism with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) is developed for predicting the unsteady flow-field around subsea pipelines. The continuity equation, momentum equations, and turbulence governing equations are embedded into the training process, and residual-gradient terms are introduced in addition to the physical-residual constraints to improve the prediction accuracy for complex flow-field variations. A dataset for the flow-field around subsea pipelines is constructed from numerical simulations, and the effects of network depth, network width, and data normalization strategies are analyzed. The results show that a network with eight hidden layers and 64 neurons per layer, combined with full normalization, achieves a favorable balance among prediction accuracy, convergence performance, and computational cost. Compared with the conventional PINN-NS model, the RANS-GPINN model converges faster and provides stronger error control in complex boundary regions, reducing the maximum error from 0.0239 to 0.0111, a decrease of approximately 53.6%. Long simulations show better model stability, aiding turbulent load assessment on ocean engineering equipment.

papers.title: Enter the Tomatrix: Model-Driven Ideotype Design for Dwarf Tomato in Vertical Farming
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial lighting accounts for most of the energy consumption in vertical farms, emphasizing the need for crops that use light efficiently. We aimed to develop and assess dwarf tomato ideotypes with architecture optimized for light absorption and carbon assimilation in vertical farming. A dynamic functional–structural plant model simulated canopy light absorption and carbon assimilation at planting densities of 35, 50, 65, and 80 plants m-2. We applied Morris sensitivity analysis to screen for influential traits, then Bayesian optimization to identify optimal trait combinations. Leaf angle, leaf curvature, and leaflet angle were the dominant architectural traits influencing canopy absorption of photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) and carbon assimilation across all planting densities. In simulations, optimized ideotypes converged towards more erect leaves with moderate curvature, improving vertical light distribution, reducing photosynthetic saturation in upper leaves, and increasing light availability deeper in the canopy. Fruits affected the canopy light balance: by the end of the simulation at 80 plants m-2, they absorbed 16% (carbon assimilation ideotype) and 23% (reference architecture) of total absorbed PAR, making fruit shading a constraint on canopy carbon gain. Simulations showed that ideotypes optimized for carbon assimilation could achieve density-dependent yield improvements, with simulated fruit dry mass increasing by up to 12% at 80 plantsm-2, compared to 2% at 35 plantsm-2. The simulations suggest that coordinated adjustments in leaf orientation traits can increase yield in dense canopies, and that ideotypes should be designed and reported for specific planting densities. This two-step workflow provides a reproducible route for ideotype design and breeding for resource-use efficiency in controlled-environment agriculture.

papers.title: Error Amplification in Koopman Predictive Control: Computable Bounds, a Conditional Lyapunov Certificate, and Horizon-Consistent Estimation
papers.abstract: Koopman model predictive control (MPC) iterates a lifted linear predictor over a horizon of tens of samples. Extended dynamic mode decomposition with control (EDMDc), however, fits that predictor by minimising only the one-step residual in the lifted space. This paper bounds the h-step output error of any lifted linear predictor by its one-step residual times an amplification factor Γh=∑j<h∥CAj∥2 that is computable from the model alone. The bound is attained for single-output systems, takes a horizon-uniform form through a scaled Lyapunov certificate, and extends to the suboptimality of the input sequence that MPC selects. The proposed HC-EDMDc minimises the rolled-out output error under a spectral-radius constraint, starts from the closed-form EDMDc solution as a warm start, and is selected by a held-out rolled-out criterion. The evaluation uses four measured benchmarks: a six-axis KUKA KR300 industrial robot, an electro-mechanical positioning system, a cascaded-tank process and the Silverbox oscillator. The one-step estimator returns a non-Schur transition matrix on 8 of 20 fits across 3 records, and its free run leaves the data range; the constraint removes this failure for at most 8.4 % of twenty-step accuracy. HC-EDMDc improves long-horizon accuracy on 2 records, reducing the twenty-step NRMSE on the cascaded tanks from 0.3431 for EDMDc + SR to 0.2827, and returns its warm start on the other 2; the size of the one-step residual does not predict which case a record falls into. Minimising εΓH collapses the predictor towards a mean-reverting model on 3 of the 4 records, and the certified bound moves opposite to the realised error on 2 of them. A valid bound is therefore not a model-selection criterion.

papers.title: Crop biophysical parameter estimation via AI-enhanced hyperspectral remote sensing
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral remote sensing has become a key approach for retrieving crop parameters related to canopy structure, physiological status, biochemical composition and productivity. However, many current methods remain centered on task-specific empirical fitting between spectral features and target parameters. Their transferability is limited when crop growth varies across phenological stages, observation scales, sensor conditions and planting systems. Hyperspectral crop-parameter retrieval is moving toward an intelligent inversion paradigm, which is jointly supported by spatio-temporal-spectral representation, mechanistic constraints and trustworthy decision-making. Accordingly, we synthesize recent progress in crop spectral-response mechanisms, satellite-airborne-ground coordinated observation, spatio-temporal consistency processing, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven retrieval models and mechanism-data fusion. Particular attention is given to the integration of hyperspectral features with crop-growth processes and canopy radiative transfer. We also examine transferable spatio-temporal-spectral representations, applicability-domain assessment and uncertainty quantification. Future advances should move beyond improving the accuracy of multi-spatio-temporal observations and instead progress toward mechanism-informed intelligent retrieval that integrates crop-growth knowledge with deep learning. This approach should explicitly represent crop growth processes, spatial heterogeneity and applicability constraints, thereby supporting more reliable crop monitoring, growth diagnosis, yield prediction and decision-making in complex agricultural systems.

papers.title: Simulating Science Communication for Vulnerable Populations: A Project-Based Learning Exercise in Undergraduate Medical Microbiology
papers.abstract: While undergraduate medical education relies heavily on traditional lectures to deliver foundational biomedical sciences, standard models frequently isolate pathogens and mechanisms from the socio-economic realities of healthcare and community communication. To address this gap, we implemented and evaluated a project-based active learning intervention conducted in a classroom setting in a Medical Microbiology course, challenging students to synthesize complex scientific literature and design educational brochures tailored for socially vulnerable populations. At the end of the academic semester, student perceptions were evaluated through an anonymous mixed-methods survey completed by 51 participants. The quantitative outcomes revealed high student satisfaction, with participants perceiving the instructions as highly transparent and the cognitive challenge as well-balanced. Notably, most of the students reported that the project successfully consolidated core microbiological content, while also stating that focusing on vulnerable communities significantly expanded their understanding of how social determinants impact infectious diseases. This strong positive feedback was also present in the thematic analysis of the open-ended responses, which showed that students highly valued practicing the translation of technical medical jargon into accessible, community-friendly language within this simulated exercise, which was conducted among peers and instructors. The primary challenges reported were operational, centered on group coordination and managing the heavy academic workload typical of the end of the semester. Overall, our findings suggest that integrating brochure design and public health context into the basic science curriculum effectively anchors microbiology to clinical and humanistic realities, fostering preliminary communication skills, teamwork, and social responsibility better than standard expository lessons.

papers.abstract: We study whether \emph{long-horizon model-based value expansion} can serve as an effective framework in pixel-based offline reinforcement learning (RL). Long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels is substantially harder than state-based environments, as the agent must learn both the representation and its dynamics, and errors from either can accumulate recursively over imagined trajectories. We introduce MAC-v2, which enables long-horizon model-based expansion from pixels by training a reconstruction-free latent world model with action chunking. By learning representations from prediction and control objectives, MAC-v2 does not need to encode control-irrelevant visual details that can hinder the dynamics prediction. Action chunking further mitigates the prediction error by reducing the number of recursive model predictions required for value expansion. Across diverse visual benchmarks including visual OGBench, MMBench2, Robomimic, and LIBERO-10, MAC-v2 achieves strong performance against model-free and model-based offline RL baselines. Our analyses show that long-horizon model-based value expansion is critical for the performance of MAC-v2, and that both action chunking and latent learning objectives are essential for reliable long-horizon latent imagination.

papers.title: Fractional physics-informed neural networks to model social media virality
papers.abstract: Existing models of social media virality either prescribe the functional form of engagement growth or assume a fixed mechanism by which past activity influences future engagement. We present a fractional physics-informed neural network that learns both the temporal memory and nonlinear growth dynamics of social media engagement, using symbolic regression to translate the learned dynamics into interpretable equations. Synthetic experiments at the deployment resolution of 24 hourly observations demonstrate that the fractional order and reaction law can be jointly recovered from clean data. Under observation noise, however, the standard pointwise physics residual drives the fractional order toward its lower bound through a scale artifact. We address this failure using a fully whitened residual that propagates observation noise through the fractional operator. Applying the framework to 348 posts from X (formerly Twitter), we find that a single-window model estimates strongly memory-dependent dynamics but fails to accurately reconstruct held-out trajectories. Partitioning the 24-hour window into four teacher-forced segments substantially improves performance, yielding segment-specific fractional orders that increase from 0.23 to 0.99 and interpretable growth laws for each phase. The segmented model reconstructs 64% of held-out trajectories within a mean squared error of 0.01, compared with 44% for the strongest of nine classical baselines. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of fractional physics-informed equation discovery to uncover interpretable engagement dynamics while highlighting the importance of noise-aware estimation and temporal segmentation.

papers.title: ShapleyOG: Fast Adaptive Shapley Value Estimation with Odd Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: Shapley values are a central tool for attribution in machine learning. Since their exact computation requires evaluating the cooperative game to be explained on exponentially many player coalitions, they are typically estimated from a limited number of evaluations. Recently, ShaplEIG has shown that adaptively selecting the coalitions to evaluate substantially improves sample efficiency over classical estimators. This, however, comes at the cost of a sequential procedure that, in every iteration, refits a Gaussian process surrogate of the game and selects the coalition with the largest expected information gain about the Shapley values. The resulting computational overhead limits its applicability to costly games with low evaluation budgets. We present fast adaptive Shapley value estimation with Odd Gaussian Processes (ShapleyOG) to overcome this limitation. ShapleyOG leverages the fact that Shapley values depend only on the odd component of the game, and we show that under paired sampling a Gaussian process surrogate on this component alone yields the same Shapley value posterior and coalition selection criterion from half as many observations. Moreover, ShapleyOG refits the surrogate only on a sparse schedule and efficiently updates the selection criterion in between, and it extends quadrature-based computation schemes to the prior covariance of the Shapley values, which allows for exact or cheaper approximate computation. In extensive experiments on diverse games, ShapleyOG matches the estimation accuracy of ShaplEIG while reducing its overhead by up to three orders of magnitude. As a result, it outperforms state-of-the-art non-adaptive estimators at equal total computation time already when a single evaluation takes a tenth of a second and a budget of a few thousand evaluations suffices, thereby widening the regime in which adaptive coalition selection is applicable and pays off.

papers.title: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification for Cancer Histopathology: Calibrated Uncertainty Under Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Reliable uncertainty quantification is essential for clinical deployment of cancer diagnosis models, yet neural networks and variational Gaussian process methods can produce overconfident predictions, particularly under the distribution shifts that arise when models trained at one hospital are applied at another. We present a scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification (GPC) framework that operates on frozen pathology foundation model embeddings (Phikon) and combines accelerated Randomly Pivoted Cholesky (RPCholesky) for low-rank kernel factorization, Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) with non-centered parameterization for posterior sampling, and a pivots-as-inducing-points scheme for prediction. This makes HMC posterior sampling in the low-rank latent representation tractable at N approximately 300,000 training points, enabling HC-based low-rank GPC on substantially larger datasets than prior MCMC-based demonstrations. We evaluate on two histopathology benchmarks for breast cancer metastasis detection: PCam and CAMELYON17-WILDS, where the latter tests calibration under hospital-level distribution shift. Compared to stochastic variational GP and neural network baselines, our method improves calibration and predictive performance - reducing expected calibration error by up to 88% and false negative rate by up to 90% - with the largest gains appearing under distribution shift, suggesting that HMC-based posterior sampling provides more trustworthy uncertainty estimates for cross-site pathology classification.

papers.title: Data-Driven Modeling of Molten Chloride Corrosion Using Static Test Data
papers.abstract: Molten chloride corrosion has been studied for decades, yet reliable prediction across different alloys, salts, and test conditions remains difficult. In this work, 291 static molten chloride corrosion experiments reported in the literature were compiled into a structured dataset and used to develop an interpretable machine-learning framework for corrosion-rate predictions. To better represent the differences in salt condition across studies, a Chloride Salt Preparation Index (CSPI) was introduced to bring the reported salt-treatment method, atmosphere control, and pre-exposure impurity condition on a common numerical scale. A blended tree-based ensemble provided the most consistent predictive performance, achieving a cross-validated \(R^2\) of 0.85 and an MAE of 0.41 mg cm\(^{-2}\) day\(^{-1}\). The graded CSPI retained more useful information than a simple purified/unpurified classification and emerged as the dominant model descriptor. Global sensitivity and SHAP analyses further identified exposure time, temperature, and alloy chemistry as important contributors to the model predictions, with several observed trends consistent with the established molten-chloride corrosion behavior. The conformal prediction intervals were well calibrated, providing an estimate of prediction uncertainty in addition to the point prediction. Overall, the framework demonstrates that historical corrosion data can support quantitative, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware prediction when experimental context is represented explicitly, while also highlighting where more consistent reporting and targeted experiments are needed to improve future molten-salt corrosion models.

papers.title: Uncertainty calibration in Bayesian M/EEG source imaging
papers.abstract: M/EEG source imaging requires accurate localization and reliable uncertainty estimates, yet posterior credible regions are rarely assessed for empirical calibration. We present a simulation-based framework for uncertainty quantification and calibration of empirical Bayesian inverse methods with closed-form conditional Gaussian posterior summaries. We compare Bayesian minimum norm (BMN) with sLORETA depth weighting and sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) with sparse basis field expansions (S-FLEX). S-FLEX allows retained coefficients to contribute nonzero marginal posterior variance at locations where voxel-wise SBL yields degenerate variances. For BMN, we derive joint source- and noise-variance updates through evidence maximization. We test whether adaptive noise learning yields near-calibrated uncertainties. Both methods retain residual miscalibration, motivating post-hoc isotonic recalibration of credible-region levels using empirical coverage. Simulations assess fixed- and free-orientation models across signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), source sparsity levels, and subject-specific head models, using oracle, baseline-estimated, and adaptively learned noise. Before recalibration, SBL+S-FLEX yields lower Wasserstein localization error, smaller posterior uncertainty, and coverage closer to nominal credibility than BMN+sLORETA. Isotonic recalibration improves both methods, with larger gains for conservative BMN+sLORETA posteriors; transfer across mismatched SNR, sparsity, and head models remains condition dependent. Noise specifications yield broadly consistent reconstruction and uncertainty trends within each estimator. In real auditory MEG data, SBL+S-FLEX provides more focal localization and tighter uncertainties than BMN+sLORETA, suggesting greater statistical power for identifying bilateral auditory sources.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Classification and Prediction of Viscoelastic Creep in Lumbar Tissues
papers.abstract: Sustained trunk flexion can cause lumbar spinal creep, a risk factor for low back disorders, but measuring creep directly is impractical outside the laboratory. This study explored whether machine learning (ML) can classify and predict creep from readily available individual and exposure characteristics. We pooled data from three published studies (44 participants, seven flexion and work-rest conditions). Creep was quantified as the change in peak lumbar flexion angle and EMG-off angle. Random forest, support vector machine, and multilayer perceptron classifiers separated low from high creep with accuracies of 0.83 to 0.85 and recall of 0.91 to 0.94. For creep magnitude, Gaussian process regression achieved the best interval coverage (PICP 91.76%), with an RMSE of 1.79°. These results suggest ML can support early monitoring of creep risk using accessible data.

papers.abstract: Reliable multimodal prognosis after acute ischemic stroke requires methods that integrate heterogeneous information under rigorous leakage control and are evaluated against strong simpler alternatives. We developed QIMCA-Net, a multimodal residual self-attention framework integrating six-channel three-dimensional computed tomography, 17 baseline clinical variables with 17 missingness indicators, and 77 quantitative whole-brain imaging biomarkers. Poor 90-day functional outcome was defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 3–6. The locked ISLES’24 cohort comprised 119 patients, including 41 with poor outcomes. Patient-level five-fold outer cross-validation with an inner training–validation hold-out split confined preprocessing and model fitting to inner-training data, while checkpoint and threshold selection and, where applicable, temperature scaling used only inner-validation data. The frozen primary QIMCA-Net achieved an out-of-fold AUROC of 0.7301 (95% CI, 0.6304–0.8280), an AUPRC of 0.5869, and a Brier score of 0.2038. Strong structured-data benchmarks remained competitive, and no model consistently dominated discrimination, positive-class retrieval, and probabilistic accuracy. Across five alternative patient-level five-fold assignments, QIMCA-Net showed a mean AUROC difference of +0.0421 relative to parameter-matched direct concatenation; however, the Nadeau–Bengio corrected interval included zero (95% CI, −0.0373 to 0.1215; p = .215). CT permutation produced negligible performance change, center-related signal was substantial, and uncertainty measures only weakly discriminated prediction errors. Lesion-auxiliary learning, Bayesian optimization, and uncertainty-aware extensions did not replace the frozen primary model. These findings support the feasibility of leakage-controlled multimodal self-attention while showing uncertain incremental architectural benefit and the need for independent external validation before clinical use.

papers.title: Green synthesis, phytochemical characterization of black shea nut cake-derived silver nanoparticles and evaluation of biological activities
papers.abstract: Sustainable nanotechnology has increased the promotion of agrowaste-based synthesis of different nanoparticles for multifarious applications. In this study, the extract of black shea nut cake (BLSNC) which is a phytochemical-rich waste from the processing of shea butter fruit was evaluated for the biosynthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) for the first time. Aqueous BLSNC extract was reacted with 1 mM silver nitrate at 30 °C under static conditions. The BLSNC-AgNPs were characterized by UV-Vis spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), selected area electron diffraction (SAED), and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). The chemical fingerprints of the nanoparticles were also studied using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). The BLSNC-AgNPs which absorbed maximally at 433 nm were crystalline and spherical-shaped having sizes of 8.4–26.5 nm. FTIR spectra revealed that compounds rich in O-H, C-O, and C = O functional groups were involved in the capping and stabilization of BLSNC-AgNPs. GC-MS identified 22 compounds in BLSNC-AgNPs which were dominated by oleic acid (10.50%), and 9-Octadecenal, (Z)- (8.15%). However, further analytical techniques such as LC-MS, HRMS, and NMR will be needed to establish the full mechanisms of phytochemical evolution during the biosynthesis of BLSNC-AgNPs. The nanoparticles showed strong antibacterial activities (65.37–88.03%) against Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Klebsiella oxytoca , Staphylococcus aureus , Proteus mirabilis , and Escherichia coli. Elevated absorbance values obtained at 260 and 280 nm showed the impacts of BLSNC-AgNPs to release DNA and proteins from the treated cells of E. coli and S. aureus . The nanoparticles completely inhibited the growth of Aspergillus species, while 69% inhibition was achieved against Candida albicans . The nanoparticles scavenged 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), nitric oxide (NO), and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) to the tune of 71.46–90.97%, inhibited α-amylase by 80.92%, and completely prevented blood clot formation, thereby showing its multifunctional biomedical potentials. Thus, shea nut cake can serve as a viable renewable material for sustainable biofabrication of AgNPs with biological activities that may be explored for biomedical applications for the promotion of circular bioeconomy and contributions to the attainment of good health and wellbeing (SDG 3).

papers.title: Diagnosing Conformal Coverage Failure Under Battery Deployment Shift for Joint State-of-Charge and State-of-Health Estimation
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction guarantees interval coverage only when calibration and deployment data are exchangeable. We test joint state-of-charge (SOC) and state-of-health (SOH) intervals when this assumption fails across cells, discharge protocols, chemistries, and an electric-vehicle (EV) driving profile, with calibration data kept separate from training and model selection. At 90% nominal, SOC coverage is 90.9% on a random cycle split but 33.0–81.4% on held-out cells, at most 0.9% on cross-protocol windows with nonzero SOC, at most 5.16% across chemistries, and 0.02% on EV-profile cells (five-seed means). SOH coverage is below nominal under every shift. Four learned baselines (recurrent, convolutional, Transformer, and physics-informed) and an equivalent-circuit Kalman filter fall short on the hardest cells. Density-ratio and optimal-transport weighting, conformalised quantile regression, and group-conditional calibration reach nominal mean coverage on no held-out cell. Recalibrating on the deployed cell’s five latest labelled cycles restores coverage to 85.5–90.3% on held-out cells without retraining, but under protocol and EV-profile shift only with intervals over half the SOC range. Under chemistry shift, optimal-transport alignment configured on labelled target data lowers SOC error by 10–59%, yet only fine-tuning with target-domain calibration restores coverage (88.0–89.3%). Source-calibrated conformal intervals are not valid under deployment shift by default.

papers.title: Redesigning Business Calculus for Active Engagement
papers.abstract: This paper presents a case study of an effort to redesign Business Calculus. In response to persistently low pass rates, we implemented a combination of research-informed practices in an experimental section of the course, including active learning, the use of technology, and an explicit focus on relevance to students' majors. Across two semesters, the redesigned section had lower DFW rates than the concurrent large-lecture sections, and students reported high levels of engagement and perceived relevance. We describe this coordinated set of reforms and present data from student surveys and interviews to provide insight into students' experiences in the redesigned course. We conclude with reflections on the redesign effort and lessons that may inform similar reforms in courses in client-discipline mathematics.

papers.title: A privacy-preserving, ethically governed blockchain–digital twin framework for auditable molecular comparison and biocomponent provenance recording
papers.abstract: Background Convalescent plasma and other biocomponent transfusions offer rapidly deployable interventions against emerging infectious diseases. However, their use is constrained by adverse-reaction risks and the absence of a shared, tamper-evident record of previously compared donor compositions and associated outcomes. Objective To develop a privacy-preserving, ethically governed blockchain-digital twin proof-of-concept for auditable molecular comparison and biocomponent provenance recording. Methods Digital-twin representations of plasma, serum and related biocomponents were instantiated using chemical formulae, SMILES strings and sequence data retrieved from ChEMBL release 33 (2023). These representations were maintained in a relational working store connected to a permissioned, Ethereum-compatible Proof-of-Authority ledger. Smart contracts recorded finalised comparisons as immutable transactions following majority validation by three randomly selected validators. Results The framework integrated molecular representation, fingerprint-based similarity matching, best-match selection and ledger-based provenance recording. Ten equations formalised twin representation, similarity matching, best-match selection, majority-consensus validation, validator-collusion probability, spam deterrence, gas cost, throughput, latency and storage overhead. Conclusion This proof-of-concept provides a formal foundation for auditable molecular comparison and traceable biocomponent records. Molecular similarity alone does not establish transfusion compatibility or clinical safety; experimental and clinical validation remain necessary before clinical application.

papers.abstract: Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motors are predominantly used in Electric Vehicle (EV) applications because of their higher efficiency, higher torque-to-weight ratio, lower maintenance requirements and capability to operate in a wide speed range. However, conventional sensor-based and traditional sensorless estimation methods experiences inaccurate performance under high-speed operating conditions because of parameter variations and nonlinear system dynamics. To overcome these limitations, this article implemented an improved sensorless Extended Kalman Filter (EKF)-based closed-loop speed estimation algorithm using Machine Learning (ML) based Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) algorithm specifically designed for high-speed applications. Performance of the implemented sensorless speed estimation scheme is experimentally validated and compared with conventional algorithms using the LAUNCHXL-F28379D development board. The experimental results indicates that the implemented method has a maximum steady-state error of 7 at 500 rpm and 8.95 at 1000 rpm between the actual motor speed and the reference speed. Furthermore, during higher operating speeds of 1500 rpm and 1600 rpm, the motor precisely tracks the reference speed.

papers.title: How Firm Is an Earwax Test for Cancer Detection? Reading the Test at Several of Its Own Settings
papers.abstract: Earwax gives off chemicals that studies in people and in dogs have linked to cancer. In the largest study so far, of 751 volunteers, the test had a sensitivity of 0.904 and a specificity of 0.880 after cross-validation. These figures describe how the test does on a group of people. They do not say how firm the verdict is for one person's sample. This note describes a way to find out. The measured data of the sample is kept exactly as it is. The settings of the analysis, such as the level at which a peak counts as present, and the settings of the classifier, are moved a little, and the verdict is read at each setting. The spread of the verdicts is the answer. A narrow spread means the verdict is firm. A wide spread means the verdict depends on a setting that should not matter, and the apparatus must be rethought before it is relied on. A computer-decided shunting action follows a wide spread. The computer decides without waiting for a person, and it moves that sample aside, for example to a repeat measurement or a confirming test, while the other samples carry on. The note covers the earwax studies, work on analysis settings in mass-spectrometry data, and methods that give a spread or a confidence from inside a model, such as Bayesian methods, Monte Carlo dropout, deep ensembles, the bootstrap and conformal prediction. For each one it explains how this method differs. The same reading applies to other tests built from the chemicals in earwax, saliva or breath. Keywords: earwax, cerumen, cancer detection, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, uncertainty, firmness of a verdict, shunting action

papers.title: Uncertainty-aware pavement performance prediction based on Gaussian process regression
papers.abstract: Deterministic pavement performance models fail to capture uncertainties inherent in the deterioration process, limiting risk-informed maintenance decision-making. This study employs Gaussian process regression (GPR), a non-parametric Bayesian inference method, to predict pavement performance while explicitly quantifying prediction uncertainty. Separate GPR models were established for eight maintenance and rehabilitation (M&R) treatments and three performance indicators, using data from 10 expressways in southeastern China. Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) were employed for feature selection, and model performance was evaluated using point and interval prediction metrics. Results show that the proposed GPR models achieved robust predictive accuracy, with coefficient of determination (R2) values exceeding 0.7 for all models and 70.83% exceeding 0.8 on testing sets. Prediction interval coverage probability (PICP) values approached the 95% confidence level with narrow intervals, confirming reliable uncertainty quantification. Out-of-sample validation on three additional expressways further confirms model generalisability. Sensitivity analysis revealed that both predictive accuracy and uncertainty quantification were largely insensitive to kernel selection. Compared with Bayesian Neural Network (BNN), random forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), GPR demonstrated more consistent prediction performance and better-calibrated uncertainty estimates. The findings highlight the effectiveness of GPR in providing uncertainty-aware predictions, offering a reliable tool for pavement maintenance management.

Seven machine learning algorithms (CatBoost, MLP, LightGBM, XGBoost, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Extra Trees, and Stacking) were benchmarked under ten-fold cross-validation and leave-one-study-out validation. Under leave-one-study-out validation the pooled R 2 of CatBoost was 0.11, so the random-split accuracy applies to mixes from studies represented in the database. A physics-informed neural network enforcing the constraint dCS/dWB < 0 reduced the share of held-out mixes with a predicted increase of CS with water-to-binder ratio (WB) from 45% to 7–21% without loss of accuracy (R 2 = 0.81–0.82). papers.title: Data-driven optimisation of laser powder bed fusion–processed biodegradable Fe35Mn
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the fabrication of patient-specific, porous, and biodegradable metallic implant architectures. However, robust processing windows remain challenging to define for biodegradable Fe–Mn alloys due to the intricate dependencies of density, surface finish, tensile properties, and corrosion response on coupled processing parameters. Here, 200 LPBF parameter combinations for Fe35Mn were generated using Latin hypercube sampling over laser power, scan speed, and hatch spacing. Relative density, top and side areal roughness, and tensile properties were then evaluated. Hierarchical Gaussian process surrogate models and multi-objective optimisation were then used to identify optimised processing parameters that balanced density, surface quality, and tensile performance. The resulting process map revealed that volumetric energy density captured the broad transition from insufficient fusion to near-dense material, but it is not sufficient to identify an optimal condition once densification had saturated. Even within the near-dense regime, surface roughness and elongation also remained strongly parameter-sensitive. The optimised processing parameters proposed here can produce tensile strengths up to 490 MPa and elongations up to 45%. Moreover, higher build rates were feasible while retaining tensile strength, but they increased surface roughness and reduced ductility, indicating that the practical productivity limit is governed mainly by surface quality and elongation. Electrochemical testing showed a corrosion rate of approximately 0.20 mm/year across the optimised conditions. Overall, the framework provides a practical LPBF process window for Fe35Mn and supports further evaluation of optimised LPBF-processed Fe35Mn for biodegradable implant applications.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning for property-damage-only crash prediction: Assessing spatial and temporal generalizability
papers.abstract: Abstract Road traffic crashes are a persistent global public health concern. In Saudi Arabia, crash rates have remained high for decades. However, most road safety studies in the country have focused on fatal and injury crashes, with limited attention to property-damage-only (PDO) incidents. Rigorous analysis of PDO crashes is essential for early risk detection, insurance considerations, and preventing escalation to more severe outcomes. Many existing machine learning (ML) models for crash prediction overlook temporal dynamics, spatial heterogeneity, and shifts in predictor importance. This study presents an explainable machine learning (XML) framework for modeling PDO crashes on intercity and rural highways in Saudi Arabia using crash data from 2017 to 2022. Six ML algorithms were evaluated using nested cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning based on the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE), a Bayesian optimization algorithm that models the search space probabilistically. XGBoost achieved the best overall performance. Temporal generalizability was assessed using a sliding-window approach, showing generally stable performance with a decline around 2020. Spatial generalizability was examined across identified hotspot regions and showed generally consistent regional performance, with slightly lower performance in major metropolitan areas. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to interpret the model. Key predictors of PDO crashes included accident type, accident cause, and the number of vehicles involved. Temporal SHAP analysis showed an increasing influence of heavy vehicles and pedestrian involvement after 2019.

papers.title: FTIR ATR Fingerprinting Coupled with Hybrid Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Olive Oil Quality Prediction
papers.abstract: Introduction Balancing olive oil quality with resource efficiency remains challenging. This study developed a Deep Hybrid Physics-Informed Neural Network (HPINN) integrating FTIR-ATR spectra, agronomic inputs, and biochemical pathway constraints to improve prediction accuracy and interpretability. Methods A two-year (2023–2024) field experiment in Meknes, Morocco, used a 3 × 3 irrigation–fertilization factorial design with three biological replicates, yielding 54 oil samples and 324 FTIR-ATR spectra. A 1D-CNN extracted spectral features, while fully connected layers predicted Total Phenolic Content (TPC), Total Flavonoid Content (TFC), DPPH antioxidant capacity, and carotenoids. Phenylpropanoid pathway relationships were incorporated as loss constraints. SHAP and Monte Carlo dropout were used for interpretation and uncertainty quantification. Validation used Leave-One-Treatment-Out Cross-Validation (LOTO-CV) and a 2023-to-2024 temporal holdout. Results LOTO-CV produced a mean Spearman ρ 2 of 0.826 across traits, compared with 0.754 for XGBoost and 0.683 for PLSR. Physics-informed regularization reduced model entropy by 37.2% and improved interannual generalizability. Ablation confirmed contributions from both CNN spectral features and biochemical constraints. SHAP identified FTIR-ATR bands consistent with relevant biochemical variation. Discussion Biochemical constraints promoted metabolically plausible predictions while retaining predictive performance, supporting their value over purely data-driven models where mechanistic knowledge is available. Conclusion Pareto optimization identified 65% ETc irrigation × 72% NPK fertilization, achieving 94% of maximum composite quality at 22% lower resource cost. HPINN provides an interpretable framework for precision olive management, with potential application to other perennial crops.

papers.title: Self-care practices among social workers in Vietnam: The role of psychological and contextual factors
papers.abstract: This study examined self-care practices and associated factors among social workers in Vietnam. A cross-sectional survey of 400 social workers was conducted, and hierarchical regression analysis assessed the contributions of sociodemographic, work-related, psychological, and contextual factors. Self-care was practiced at a moderate level and varied across domains. Psychological and contextual resources, particularly self-efficacy, compassion satisfaction, active learning, and perceived social support, were significant predictors, whereas sociodemographic and occupational characteristics showed limited associations. Compassion fatigue became significant after psychological and contextual factors were considered. These findings highlight self-care as a multidimensional process shaped by individual resources and supportive work environments.
